summary: An imported disconnected graph is scored as 100% connection quality with a small finite ASPL, because the app discards the core's `connected` flag (and never calls `largestComponentFraction`). `allPairsSummary` averages ASPL over REACHABLE pairs only, so a split roster yields a finite, misleadingly-low aspl; `asplGap` then goes negative (the reachable-pairs mean beats the Moore bound computed for the whole n) and `clampQuality` pins quality to 1.
failure: Import a hand-edited file of two disjoint triangles — people(6), edges [[0,1],[1,2],[2,0],[3,4],[4,5],[5,3]] — a regular, DISCONNECTED graph (two groups that never meet). importGraph returns metrics {quality:1, aspl:1, diameter:1, regular:true, degreeMax:2}. QualityPanel then displays 'avg hops 1.0 / most steps 1 / connection quality 100 — everyone's well-linked' and the rail says '6 people · 2 buddies each'. Reproduced identically for two disjoint K4s (quality 100%, aspl 1), triangle+isolated vertex (quality 100%, aspl 1, degMin 0), and an edgeless roster (quality 100%, diameter 0). Every case flatly contradicts the product's core promise ('the whole group stays closely connected'), and the aspl/diameter labels ('between ANY two people') are literally false when some pairs are unreachable. Generation cannot hit this (the ring seed is always connected), so it is import-only — but F6 import of hand-edited files is a shipped feature that claims to 're-measure honestly'.
remediation: Consume the core's connectivity signal instead of dropping it. In importGraph, take `summary.connected` (already returned by allPairsSummary) and/or `largestComponentFraction(g)` and thread it into the view. When not connected, treat whole-roster ASPL/diameter/quality as undefined for the whole graph: force aspl/diameter to null (they are only meaningful over reachable pairs) and quality to 0 (or expose a distinct 'disconnected — N separate groups / X% in the largest group' state) rather than clamping a negative asplGap up to 1. Add a `connected: boolean` (or `largestComponentFraction`) field to the Metrics shape and surface it in QualityPanel/the rail so the UI can say 'split into groups' instead of 'everyone's well-linked'. Also fix the now-wrong comments in model.ts:17 and model.ts:50 ('null when disconnected') — allPairsSummary returns Infinity only when NO pair is reachable (edgeless / n<=1), not for a disconnected-but-edged graph.
testUpgrade: Class = disconnected/partitioned imported graphs must never read as optimal or fully-linked. Add a parameterized (table-driven) test in importExport.roundtrip.test.ts over disconnected topologies — two disjoint triangles (regular), two disjoint K4s (regular), triangle+isolated vertex (irregular, degMin 0), and an edgeless roster — asserting for each that EITHER import is refused OR (metrics.connected === false AND metrics.quality < 1 AND metrics.aspl === null). Complement with a property/fuzz generator that builds two independent connected components of random sizes and edge sets and asserts the same invariant, so future component counts/shapes are covered. The existing round-trip and 'scores from actual graph' tests only exercise CONNECTED graphs (generated k-regular graphs, single cycles, K4), so they are structurally blind to this class.

summary: An import that lands while a generate/reroll is still in flight is silently overwritten when the worker result finally arrives.
failure: A graph already exists so QualityPanel + its Import button are rendered. User clicks Different arrangement -> handleReroll calls bg.generate, setting pending.current={names,settings} and starting the worker (status=running; the OLD view keeps showing so Import stays clickable). Before the worker replies the user imports a file -> applyImported -> bg.loadView(v) sets view=imported graph; loadView touches neither pending.current nor consumed. The worker then posts its result; id still == latestId so useGenerationWorker delivers it -> gen.status=done, gen.result is a fresh object != consumed.current, pending.current still non-null -> the effect (lines 20-25) runs setView(viewFromResult(pending...)) and replaces the imported graph with the regenerated one. Imported file is discarded; displayed graph is wrong.
remediation: Make loadView supersede in-flight generation: in loadView set pending.current=null (and/or bump a monotonic epoch captured in generate() and re-checked in the effect) so a late worker response for a superseded request is dropped. The existing `consumed` ref only blocks re-applying an already-consumed result, not a first-time result arriving after an import.
testUpgrade: renderHook(useBuddyGraph) with a mocked useGenerationWorker exposing status/result. Parameterize over orderings of {generate-start, loadView(import), worker-message-arrives}; assert that whenever loadView occurs after generate-start but before the worker result, the final view equals the imported view for every ordering in the class.

summary: An imported disconnected/edgeless graph displays 100% connection quality, contradicting its own disconnected metrics.
failure: importGraph({version:1, people:[P0..P3], edges:[]}) yields metrics {degreeMin:0, degreeMax:0, aspl:null, diameter:0, quality:1} (reproduced: [0,0,null,+0,1]). quality(aspl,n,degreeMax) calls asplGap(Infinity,n,0); mooreLowerBounds returns asplLb=0 for k<=0, so asplGap returns 0 (no-bound), and clampQuality(0)=1. UI then shows the gauge at 100% while the rail says '0 buddies each' and avg/max hops show em-dash/0 -- a fully unconnected roster reads as the theoretical best, violating the import path's honest-re-measure claim. Same false-100% for any degreeMax===0.
remediation: In model.ts quality(), guard non-finite aspl (or degreeMax===0) to return 0 (or null) before delegating to asplGap, so asplGap's 'no valid bound => gap 0' cannot collapse to clampQuality(0)=1. Core stays untouched; this is a UI interpretation fix.
testUpgrade: Parameterize importGraph over degenerate files -- {edges:[] with n in [1,4,50]}, {one isolated vertex among a connected remainder}, {two disjoint components} -- asserting metrics.quality===0 (or null) whenever metrics.aspl===null, and quality in (0,1] only when aspl is finite.

summary: Imported settings.buddies is clamped only on the low side (>=2), never bounded above, so a crafted high-degree import injects an arbitrarily large k (up to n-1) that later generation consumes, hanging the worker for hours and wedging all future generation.
failure: Import a star file: {version:1, people:[...2000], edges:[[0,1],[0,2],...,[0,1999]]}. It passes every gate (m=1999, work product ~8M < MAX_IMPORT_WORK=40M). degreeMax=1999, so sanitizeSettings sets settings.buddies=1999 (App.tsx:48 handleReroll, or the modal Generate with an untouched stepper). That calls buildBuddyGraph(2000,1999) in the worker, which is uncapped on work (only n<=5000 checked). Measured dense-k growth: n=200->0.9s, n=400->15s, n=600->80s; n=2000,k=1999 is hours. Worker processes messages synchronously, so the runaway job also blocks every subsequent generate/reroll until page reload.
remediation: Clamp imported buddies to the UI-supported range in sanitizeSettings, e.g. buddies = Math.min(12, Math.max(2, candidate)) (mirror SettingsControls' clamp(k,2,12)); and/or clamp k in useBuddyGraph.generate before postMessage as defense-in-depth. Optionally terminate+recreate the worker when a new request supersedes a running one so a runaway job can't wedge the session. Ideally also add a work cap to the core's unconstrained buildBuddyGraph (n*min(k,n-1)) mirroring MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK.
testUpgrade: Parameterized adversarial-import table (star/hub, near-complete, and files with declared settings.buddies in {13, 100, n-1, 1e6}) asserting the k the app would actually generate with (sanitizeSettings(...).buddies, and the value passed by handleReroll/handleGenerate) is bounded to the supported range (<=12); plus a fuzz generator emitting random degree sequences and declared buddies asserting sanitizeSettings output stays within [2,12]. Guards the CLASS of untrusted-file fields flowing unclamped into generation cost.

summary: A fully disconnected imported graph with zero edges reports 100% connection quality because asplGap short-circuits to 0 when degreeMax=0 (k=0), while aspl displays as '—'.
failure: importGraph({version:1, people:[6 people], edges:[]}) yields aspl=Infinity, degreeMin=degreeMax=0. quality(Infinity, n, 0) -> asplGap(Infinity,n,0) returns 0 (asplLb<=0 branch) -> clampQuality(0)=1 -> gauge shows 100% 'everyone's well-linked' for an all-isolated roster. Reproduced via ringweave allPairsSummary+asplGap.
remediation: In model.ts quality(): return 0 when !Number.isFinite(aspl) (disconnected / n<=1), before delegating to asplGap, so a non-finite ASPL never scores as optimal regardless of degreeMax/k.
testUpgrade: Parameterized table of disconnected imports (edgeless roster, a perfect matching, two disjoint cliques, single isolated vertex among a group) asserting metrics.quality===0 whenever metrics.aspl===null; a property test: for any imported graph, quality>0 implies aspl is finite. Guards the CLASS of disconnected/degenerate graphs being scored as high-quality.

summary: Connection-quality reads 100% for a fully-disconnected / edgeless imported graph because asplGap treats degree-0 (k=0) as "no Moore bound => optimal".
failure: Import {version:1, people:[50 names], edges:[]} (or any hand-edited file where nobody is connected, or n<=1). Traced + reproduced: assembleMetrics calls quality(raw.aspl=Infinity, n, degreeMax=0); mooreLowerBounds(n,0) hits the k<=0 branch and returns asplLb=0; asplGap returns 0 (asplLb<=0 guard); clampQuality(1-0)=1. Ran importGraph for n=1,2,50 -> degreeMax=0, aspl=null, diameter=0, quality=1. QualityPanel then shows avg hops "—", most steps "0", and a 100% gauge labeled "everyone's well-linked" for 50 isolated people. Note the asymmetry: a DISCONNECTED graph that still has edges (degreeMax>=1) correctly scores 0 because asplLb>0 makes asplGap=Infinity; only the degreeMax===0 / n<=1 corner is mis-scored, and model.ts already normalizes aspl to null for display but forgot to normalize quality the same way.
remediation: Normalize quality at the same boundary that normalizes aspl. In model.ts `quality()` add a guard for non-finite ASPL: `export function quality(aspl:number,n:number,k:number){ if(!Number.isFinite(aspl)) return 0; return clampQuality(asplGap(aspl,n,k)); }` (or gate it in assembleMetrics: `quality: Number.isFinite(raw.aspl) ? quality(...) : 0`). This makes an edgeless/disconnected graph score 0 like the with-edges disconnected case already does. Also update the assembleMetrics doc-comment (lines 64-70), which claims quality "matches the core's own asplGap" without noting the k=0 degeneracy it silently inherits.
testUpgrade: Parameterize a test over graphs whose ASPL is non-finite: `for (const [n,edges] of [[2,[]],[50,[]],[6,[[0,1],[2,3]]] /* two components */,[1,[]]]) expect(importGraph({version:1,people:names(n),edges}).metrics.quality).toBe(0)`. Guards the CLASS (any disconnected/edgeless import must not report a positive quality), not just the 50-isolated-people input.

summary: BuddyGraphFile.meta.metrics re-declares the full model.Metrics shape by hand, and importGraph never reads meta at all — it is a write-only mirror that can silently drift from Metrics.
failure: A future contributor adds a field to `Metrics` in model.ts (e.g. a new score). exportGraph.ts:29 writes `metrics: view.metrics` into meta.metrics, but schema.ts's hand-written meta.metrics type won't include the new field, so `exportGraph`'s return type and the file's documented schema disagree with what is actually serialized — and no test/typecheck catches it because import discards meta entirely (importGraph.ts recomputes from edges). Verified by grep: `meta` is referenced only in exportGraph.ts (write) and schema.ts (type); importGraph.ts never reads f.meta.
remediation: Make the schema reference the single source of truth instead of copying it: `meta: { app: "BuddyGraph"; metrics: import('../model').Metrics }` (or export a `type FileMetrics = Metrics` from model and use it in both places). Then adding a Metrics field can't leave the file schema stale. Optionally add a one-line comment on schema.meta noting it is informational/write-only (import re-measures).
testUpgrade: Add a structural test that asserts the serialized meta.metrics has exactly the keys of a produced Metrics object: `expect(Object.keys(exportGraph(view).meta.metrics).sort()).toEqual(Object.keys(view.metrics).sort())` — fails the moment Metrics gains/loses a field that the schema mirror misses.

summary: handleReroll resets `selected` but not `hovered`; every other graph-replacing path (handleGenerate, applyImported) resets both, so the reroll path is an inconsistent outlier.
failure: Pointer physically rests over a node (so onMouseEnter set hovered=i) while the user activates "Different arrangement" via keyboard (Tab+Enter, which does not fire onMouseLeave). Reroll regenerates with the same n, so index i is still in-range; GraphCanvas then lights node i's buddy set from the NEW graph — a highlight the user never asked for on a person they aren't pointing at. No crash (adjacency[focus] is guarded), but the highlight is misleading and diverges from the reset done on generate/import. Marked PLAUSIBLE: the mouse-driven path clears hovered before the button click, so only the keyboard-while-hovering path exhibits it.
remediation: Add `setHovered(null);` in handleReroll (App.tsx around line 53), matching handleGenerate/applyImported. Better: extract the shared reset (`setSelected(null); setHovered(null);`) into one helper called by all three graph-replacing handlers so a fourth entry point can't forget it.
testUpgrade: A component/integration test that sets hovered, triggers each graph-replacing action (generate, reroll, import) and asserts hovered===null after — parameterized over the three actions so the CLASS "replacing the graph clears transient selection/hover" is enforced uniformly, not just for generate/import.

summary: When a disconnected import's largest component is >=99.5% of the roster, Math.round makes the panel display '100% are in the largest group' while simultaneously saying 'not everyone's connected' — a self-contradiction, and a number that disagrees with the core's actual largestComponentFraction (<1).
failure: Import n=200 with a connected path on vertices 0..198 and vertex 199 isolated -> core largestComponentFraction = 199/200 = 0.995, connected=false. QualityPanel renders: "not everyone's connected — 100% are in the largest group". (Reproduced: any lcf in [0.995,1) rounds up to 100 via Math.round(99.5)=100.)
remediation: For the disconnected branch, floor instead of round so the shown percentage can never reach 100 while connected===false, e.g. compute `const largestPct = m.connected ? 100 : Math.min(99, Math.floor(m.largestComponentFraction*100));` (or clamp the rounded value to 99 when !m.connected). The gauge quality percentage is unaffected (0 when disconnected).
testUpgrade: Class: 'a percentage the UI derives from a connectivity fraction must not read 100% while connected===false'. Add a parameterized/property test over disconnected imports whose largest component spans [0.990,0.999] of n (e.g. n in {200,500,1000} with 1..3 isolated vertices) asserting the *formatted* largest-group percentage is < 100 whenever metrics.connected is false. Existing importExport.roundtrip disconnected cases only use lcf<=0.75, so they never exercise the rounding boundary.

summary: A 1-person import yields connected=true but quality=0 and aspl/diameter=null (no reachable pairs), so the panel shows 'connection quality — everyone's well-linked' next to a 0% gauge and '—' hops, a contradictory readout.
failure: importGraph({version:1, people:[{id:0,name:'Solo'}], edges:[]}) -> metrics {connected:true, quality:0, aspl:null, diameter:null}. Panel: text 'everyone's well-linked' with gauge showing 0. (Reproduced.)
remediation: Treat the no-measurable-pairs case as its own display state: when metrics.aspl===null (or n<2) show a neutral 'not enough people to score' label instead of the connected 'well-linked' copy — e.g. branch on `m.aspl == null` before the `m.connected` ternary. Alternatively have assembleMetrics report connected=false (or a `measurable` flag) for n<2 so the honest-disconnection copy is used.
testUpgrade: Class: 'quality===0 must never be paired with a positive/optimistic connectivity label'. Parameterized test over degenerate rosters (n=1 with edges:[], and any import where metrics.aspl===null) asserting the QualityPanel-selected label is the non-'well-linked' variant. Current 'disconnected/degenerate' suite checks metric values but not the n=1 connected-yet-unscored combination, and no test asserts the rendered label.

summary: loadView supersedes an in-flight generation by clearing `pending`, but does not reset the worker's `running` status, so the App's "Generating…" overlay stays up over the freshly-imported graph until the superseded worker finishes.
failure: With a view already shown, click "Different arrangement" on a large roster (e.g. n=5000, ~13s in the worker) -> status="running", busy overlay shown. Before it finishes, click Import and load a file. loadView sets view=imported and pending=null (so the late worker result is correctly dropped), but gen.status stays "running". App.tsx:147 keeps a false "Generating…" overlay over the imported graph until the superseded worker finally returns (seconds later). View preservation is correct; only the indicator is wrong.
remediation: Have loadView also move status out of "running": expose a reset()/cancel() on useGenerationWorker that sets {status:'idle', result:null} (bump latestId so the in-flight response is dropped there too) and call it from loadView alongside clearing pending. That hides the overlay and makes supersession explicit at the worker layer instead of only via the pending-ref guard.
testUpgrade: In useBuddyGraph.test.tsx extend the supersede case: after loadView(imported) during a mocked 'running' generation, assert result.current.status !== 'running' AND view === imported. Parameterize over {import before worker replies, import after} so the class 'no stale running indicator survives a supersede' is guarded, not just view preservation.

summary: The exported quality(aspl,n,k) helper (scored at target k) is a second, divergent implementation of the display quality that assembleMetrics computes inline at degreeMax; they disagree for irregular graphs and the tests exercise only the off-path helper.
failure: For an irregular generated graph (odd n*k, e.g. n=25,k=3 where one vertex has degree 4), assembleMetrics (model.ts:81) scores clampQuality(asplGap(aspl,n,degreeMax=4)) -- the shipped display value -- while exported quality(aspl,n,3) (model.ts:47, what quality.test.ts:8 checks) scores at k=3. They differ, and the shipped path is never asserted for an irregular case: a maintainer 'fixing' quality() changes no pixel, and a regression in assembleMetrics's inline formula still passes quality.test.ts.
remediation: Make assembleMetrics call a single quality-from-degree helper (quality(raw.aspl, n, raw.degreeMax)) so there is one source of truth, and either drop the k-taking overload or rename it to signal it is the target-k variant not used for display.
testUpgrade: Parameterize quality.test.ts over regular AND irregular rosters (e.g. (24,4) regular and (25,3)/(15,3) irregular): assert viewFromResult(...).metrics.quality === clampQuality(asplGap(r.aspl, n, r.degreeMax)) for every case, pinning the shipped formula and the degreeMax-vs-k divergence.

summary: A dense imported graph passes every round-4 import cap yet triggers a multi-second main-thread freeze: the size gates bound the BFS metric cost but nothing bounds the synchronous force layout or the SVG render, which scale with EDGE count while FORCE_MAX_N gates only on node count.
failure: Import file: {version:1, people:[430 people], edges:[all 92,235 K430 pairs]}. All gates pass (people 430<=2000; edges 92,235<=100,000; product 430*(430+92235)=39,845,950<40,000,000). importGraph returns a 92,235-edge GraphView. GraphCanvas.tsx:58 computes forceLayout(430, 92235) unconditionally on mount; because n=430<FORCE_MAX_N=1000 the FULL d3-force sim runs -> measured 1,543 ms on the UI thread. React then mounts ~92k <line> + 430 <g> elements, and every hover re-renders all of them (edgeClass/nodeClass recomputed per element). Metric cost itself was only 258 ms, so MAX_IMPORT_WORK 'kept the tab responsive' for the wrong subsystem.
remediation: Add an edge/render budget that runs alongside MAX_IMPORT_WORK: (1) gate FORCE_MAX_N on edges.length too (fall back to ring when m exceeds a few thousand), and (2) cap or virtualize rendered edges in GraphCanvas (or refuse import above a MAX_RENDER_EDGES ~ 5-8k distinct edges) so a near-complete graph can't freeze layout+render+hover. The product cap bounds O(n*(n+m)) BFS but not O(m) DOM/layout.
testUpgrade: Parameterized dense-import table of K_n / near-complete graphs sampled AT the work-budget boundary (n in {200,300,430}), asserting the resulting view.edges length is within a render budget OR that forceLayout falls back to ring; plus a fuzz generator over (n, density) that fails if forceLayout is invoked (n<=FORCE_MAX_N) while edges exceed the render budget.

summary: The app admits rosters up to MAX_NAMES=5000, but unconstrained generation (ringGreedy) is ~O(n^3); feasibility grossly understates it ('may take a few seconds' above 800) and the single worker has no cancellation, so a stale long run blocks all later generate/reroll.
failure: A 1000-name roster (well under the 5000 cap; the >800 warning still says 'a few seconds') posts buildBuddyGraph(1000,12) to the worker: measured 29,500 ms. n=2000 exceeded 90 s (timeout). Because useGenerationWorker.generate only posts a message and the stale-id logic drops the RESULT (not the computation), a subsequent reroll queues behind the busy worker and cannot run for ~30 s+. Off-main-thread so the UI doesn't freeze, but the generation subsystem is effectively DoS'd by an ordinary large roster and the preflight time estimate is off by >10x.
remediation: Lower the app's generation ceiling to a size that finishes in a few seconds (measure a real budget, e.g. n s.t. wall-clock < ~3 s), fix the LARGE_ROSTER threshold/wording to reflect the real cost, and add worker cancellation (terminate + recreate the worker when a superseding request arrives) so a stale run can't monopolize it.
testUpgrade: A timing/parameterized test over n in {500,1000,2000} asserting buildBuddyGraph completes under an agreed wall-clock budget (or that the app refuses/warns accurately above it), plus a hook test that a second generate() supersedes an in-flight run rather than queueing behind it.

summary: parseRoster's tokenization (split/map/filter) materializes the full token array of the whole 2 MB-capped text before MAX_NAMES caps the dedup loop, so per-keystroke cost is O(chars), not O(names).
failure: Paste ~2 MB of comma-separated tokens into the roster textarea (readFileText allows 8 MB drops; parseRoster slices to MAX_PARSE_CHARS=2M). RosterModal re-runs parseRoster via useMemo on every keystroke: measured ~177 ms per keystroke even though only 1 unique name results, because split(/[\n,]/).map(trim).filter processes ~700k tokens before the MAX_NAMES=5000 break in the dedup loop ever applies. Janky but recoverable (bounded by the 2M char cap).
remediation: Bound tokenization by names, not chars: stop splitting/collecting once MAX_NAMES distinct names are found (e.g. incremental scan, or a capped split), so per-keystroke work is proportional to the kept names rather than the pasted character count.
testUpgrade: Parameterized large-paste timing table (varying token size and dup ratio at the 2M-char cap) asserting parseRoster runs under a fixed budget and never allocates more than ~O(MAX_NAMES) intermediate tokens.

summary: The connection-quality caption branches only on `m.connected`, so a connected-but-poorly-linked graph shows a near-zero gauge while the text asserts everyone is well-linked.
failure: Import a star graph (e.g. 200 people, all edged only to person 0). Verified with the core: connected=true, aspl=1.99, asplGap=0.99 => quality rounds to 1/100. QualityPanel renders the gauge as `1` but the caption reads "connection quality — everyone's well-linked" because it only checks m.connected, not m.quality. The round-4 fix made the DISconnected case honest but left the connected-yet-terrible case overstating. (The n=1 edgeless import is the same shape: connected:true, quality:0, caption still 'well-linked'.)
remediation: Base the caption on both connectivity and the score. Extract a pure `connectionSummary(m: Metrics): string` (e.g. disconnected -> "…N% in the largest group"; connected && quality < ~0.5 -> "everyone's connected, but loosely linked"; else -> "everyone's well-linked") and render that, so the words can't contradict the gauge.
testUpgrade: Parameterized test over [tight cycle C6 (high q), long path, star K(1,n-1) (connected, q~0), two disjoint triangles (disconnected)] asserting connectionSummary never returns the 'well-linked' phrasing when m.quality is below the threshold or m.connected is false.

summary: The buddies-per-person range [2,12] is hardcoded in three independent places with only a prose 'mirrors' comment tying them together, so a change to the UI stepper silently desyncs the import clamp.
failure: importGraph.ts:6-7 defines MIN_BUDDIES=2/MAX_BUDDIES=12 ('mirrors SettingsControls' stepper range'); SettingsControls.tsx:18 clamps with literal `2,12` and the JSX uses min={2}/max={12}. A future contributor who raises the stepper max to 16 in SettingsControls will leave importGraph's sanitizeSettings still clamping imported buddies to 12 — a hand-authored file's declared k=15 would be silently rounded to 12 while the live UI allows 15, a mismatch with no compile error.
remediation: Export a single source of truth, e.g. `export const BUDDY_MIN = 2; export const BUDDY_MAX = 12;` from model.ts (or a shared io/limits.ts), and consume it in SettingsControls' clamp/min/max and importGraph's sanitizeSettings instead of the literals.
testUpgrade: In the existing 'untrusted settings.buddies is clamped' suite, import the shared BUDDY_MAX constant and assert the clamp ceiling equals it (rather than a hardcoded 12), so the test fails if the two ranges ever diverge.

summary: `quality()` is exercised only by tests: production re-inlines `clampQuality(asplGap(...))` in assembleMetrics, and quality()'s own doc claims the Moore-gap is 'never re-derived in the UI' — which the inline re-derivation contradicts.
failure: quality() (model.ts:47) is imported by app/test only (grep shows no src caller). assembleMetrics (model.ts:81) computes `measurable ? clampQuality(asplGap(raw.aspl, n, raw.degreeMax)) : 0`, a second copy of the same scorer. If someone tweaks the clamp or the '0 when non-finite' rule in quality() (the documented canonical scorer), assembleMetrics — the path the UI actually renders — silently keeps the old behavior, and the comment 'never re-derived in the UI' actively misleads the reader into thinking there is one implementation.
remediation: Have assembleMetrics call the canonical helper under its connectivity gate: `quality: measurable ? quality(raw.aspl, n, raw.degreeMax) : 0`. Then correct/remove the 'never re-derived in the UI' clause on quality()'s doc so it matches reality (it IS the single scorer, called by assembleMetrics).
testUpgrade: Fuzz test: for random small graphs (varied n, degree, connectivity) assert `assembleMetrics(...).quality === (measurable ? quality(aspl, n, degreeMax) : 0)`, guarding against the two scorers drifting.

summary: `degreeExtent` is a byte-for-byte duplicate of the core's private helper in lib/src/core/index.ts:314-323.
failure: importGraph.ts:28-37 reimplements the exact loop-based min/max in lib index.ts:314-323 (same 'avoid arg-spread limits' rationale). Two copies means a future fix (e.g. handling an empty-degree edge case differently) has to be found and applied twice; the app copy is easy to miss because it lives under io/.
remediation: Export `degreeExtent` from the core (it is already a reusable, contract-free utility) and import it in importGraph, or lift it into a shared app util so there is one definition. Given the core already exposes g.degrees(), a thin exported extremum helper is the cleaner seam.
testUpgrade: A shared unit test on the single degreeExtent (empty array -> [0,0]; mixed sequence -> correct min/max) referenced from both packages, so the behavior is pinned in one place.

summary: viewFromResult hardcodes connected:true and largestComponentFraction:1 because BuddyResult carries no connectivity field, so the false-100% path the import fix guards against is only assumed-away, never measured, on the generation path.
failure: buildBuddyGraph's BuddyResult exposes aspl/diameter/girth/degreeMin/Max but NOT connected/largestComponentFraction (only ConstrainedBuddyResult.report has them, lib/src/core/index.ts). If a future core change ever left the unconstrained output disconnected, viewFromResult would report connected:true, lcf:1 and score quality from a finite reachable-pairs ASPL via degreeMax -> a false 100% 'everyone's well-linked' -- exactly the disconnected-import failure assembleMetrics was hardened against. The generation path trusts a documented but uncross-checked invariant.
remediation: Lib-first (per app/CLAUDE.md): add connected and largestComponentFraction to BuddyResult (the worker already computes allPairsSummary, whose Summary carries `connected`), then pass them through in viewFromResult instead of literals, so both view-model producers measure connectivity identically.
testUpgrade: Add a parity property test: for random (n,k), build a Graph from buildBuddyGraph(...).edges and assert viewFromResult(...).metrics.{connected,largestComponentFraction,quality} equals importGraph on the same edges -- the two GraphView producers must agree on connectivity/quality for identical edge sets, so an assumed-vs-measured divergence fails.

summary: sanitizeSettings clamps buddies to the UI range [2,12] (round-4 fix) but leaves minSeparation unclamped (any integer >= 2 from the file flows through), an incomplete version of the same untrusted-field-into-generation hardening.
failure: Import {settings:{minSeparation: 999999999, buddies:4, seed:1, polish:'auto'}}. sanitizeSettings returns minSeparation=999999999 unchanged (line 47-50 only checks >=2). A later reroll passes it to buildBuddyGraph. No hang today (ringGreedy clamps curMind=min(mind, floor(n/2))), so this is an integrity/consistency gap, not a crash: the app silently uses a separation target the UI stepper (clamped [2,12]) can never express, and it is the exact class the buddies clamp was added to close.
remediation: Clamp minSeparation to the UI range [2,12] in sanitizeSettings, mirroring buddies, so no imported field bypasses the stepper's bounds and no future core change on minSeparation can be driven out of range from a file.
testUpgrade: Extend the existing 'untrusted settings clamped' table to minSeparation (values 1, 13, 100, 1e9, NaN, '5') asserting the sanitized value is an integer in [2,12].

summary: handleReroll refuses with a hardcoded 'adjust buddy count' message that ignores the real feasibility reason, so a large imported roster is told to do something that can't fix it.
failure: Import a valid file with 1001-2000 people (allowed: MAX_IMPORT_N=2000, and the rail's 'Different arrangement' button is shown for any view). Click it. feasibility(1500, k) returns canGenerate=false with messages=["That's 1500 people — the most this tool generates for is 1000."], but handleReroll discards feasibility().messages and flashes "Can't re-arrange this roster with the current buddy count — use Edit people to adjust it." The user is directed to change the buddy count, which will never make a 1500-person roster generatable (the ceiling is on n, MAX_ROSTER_N=1000). Same mismatch for the n<k+1 case wording vs the actual too-many/too-few reason.
remediation: In handleReroll, surface the actual reason from the feasibility result instead of a fixed string, e.g. `const f = feasibility(names.length, s.buddies); if (!f.canGenerate) { flash(f.messages[0] ?? "Can't re-arrange this roster — use “Edit people” to adjust it."); return; }`
testUpgrade: Class: every UI gate that blocks an action must show the gate's own reason, not a canned one. Add a table-driven test over the reroll gate covering (too-many-people n>MAX_ROSTER_N, too-few n<k+1, k<2 after an import-clamp edge) asserting the flashed/returned message equals feasibility(n,k).messages[0] for each — a generator that walks n across the MAX_ROSTER_N boundary and k across [1,BUDDY_MAX] would also catch future divergence. The existing feasibility.test.ts checks canGenerate/messages in isolation but nothing asserts App surfaces those messages on reroll.

summary: minSeparation (degrees of separation, a distinct domain concept) is clamped to the buddies-per-person range [BUDDY_MIN, BUDDY_MAX] in three places, coupling two unrelated knobs to one constant pair.
failure: The core treats minSeparation (mind, default 5, valid up to floor(n/2)) as independent from k. But setMinSep clamps to [BUDDY_MIN=2, BUDDY_MAX=12] (SettingsControls.tsx:21), the number input hard-wires max={BUDDY_MAX} (SettingsControls.tsx:47), and importGraph.sanitizeSettings clamps minSeparation to [BUDDY_MIN, BUDDY_MAX] (importGraph.ts:36). Concrete obstruction: the next reasonable change -- raising BUDDY_MAX to allow more buddies -- silently widens the minSeparation input's ceiling for an unrelated reason; conversely, wanting minSeparation>12 on a large roster (where floor(n/2) is far above 12) forces editing a buddies-count constant. The two features cannot evolve independently. No wrong output today (5 is in [2,12]); it obstructs the next change.
remediation: Introduce SEPARATION_MIN/SEPARATION_MAX constants in model.ts (or derive the upper bound from n, e.g. min(cap, floor(n/2))) and use them in setMinSep, the input's max attribute, and sanitizeSettings. Leave BUDDY_MIN/MAX for buddies only. Cost ~2 constants + 3 one-line edits; benefit: the two knobs evolve independently.
testUpgrade: Parameterized test asserting the minSeparation clamp bounds derive from SEPARATION_* constants, not BUDDY_*: change a hypothetical BUDDY_MAX and assert the sanitized/clamped minSeparation range is unaffected (guards the class 'two knobs must not share one bound').

summary: An imported person whose name contains a comma is silently split into two people if the user opens 'Edit people' and regenerates, because the roster textarea round-trips through a comma/newline parser.
failure: importGraph accepts arbitrary name strings, so a file with a person named 'Doe, Jane' yields names=['Doe, Jane', ...]. Clicking 'Edit people' feeds initialText = names.join('\n') (App.tsx:139) into RosterModal; parseRoster's TOKEN=/[^\n,]+/g (parseRoster.ts:16) treats the comma as a delimiter, so a regenerate produces 'Doe' and 'Jane' as two separate people -- a silent roster corruption the paste path can never introduce but import can. Niche (import + Edit + regenerate) but real.
remediation: Reject/normalize commas in imported names at the import boundary, or make the modal's initialText path lossless (pass the imported names array to the modal directly instead of re-serializing to comma-parseable text). Cost a few lines; benefit: closes a silent data-loss path for imported/hand-authored files.
testUpgrade: Round-trip test: importGraph a file with a name containing a comma, then feed names.join('\n') through parseRoster and assert the person count and names are preserved (guards the class 'import->edit->regenerate must not change the roster').

summary: App embeds a full transient-notice/toast subsystem (state + effect + flash timer + inline-styled render) alongside generation orchestration, selection, hover, layout, and import plumbing -- the clearest separable seam in the god-component.
failure: App owns setNotice/flash (App.tsx:25,34-37), the error-to-notice effect (29-32), and a hand-styled fixed-position toast div (161-173). Adding a second transient message kind (a success toast distinct from an error banner, or stacking) means growing this inline block and its ad-hoc lifecycle inside App rather than extending a dedicated component. Borderline-acceptable at M2, but it is the one concern that will resist the next UI-message change.
remediation: Extract a useNotice() hook (state + flash + auto-clear + the bg.error bridge) and a <Notice/> component; App keeps only orchestration and passes messages in. Cost ~30-line extraction; benefit: a second message type becomes additive, not an edit to App's render.
testUpgrade: A test for the extracted useNotice hook covering flash auto-clear, the 'don't clobber a newer message' guard, and clear-on-new-run -- parameterized over message sources (error vs. flash) so a future message type is covered by construction.

summary: Roster textarea stores untruncated text; only the parse is capped, not the stored/rendered string.
failure: readFile() does setText(await readFileText(file)) with a file up to MAX_FILE_BYTES=8 MB, and the controlled <textarea value={text} onChange={setText}> also accepts an unbounded PASTE (paste is not gated by readFileText's 8 MB). parseRoster() is bounded (MAX_PARSE_CHARS=500k) but the React state string and the DOM textarea value are not. Loading an ~8 MB roster (or pasting tens of MB) leaves a multi-MB controlled textarea; every subsequent keystroke calls setText(new huge string), re-renders, and re-syncs the giant DOM value + re-slices 500k in the useMemo — janking/freezing the modal on each keystroke. This is the exact 'per-keystroke recompute over unbounded input' class the round-5 MAX_PARSE_CHARS fix only half-closed: it bounded the parse, not the text the parse (and the DOM) hold.
remediation: Truncate at the storage boundary, not just the parse: in readFile() and the textarea onChange, cap stored text to ~MAX_PARSE_CHARS (e.g. text.slice(0, MAX_PARSE_CHARS)) so state, DOM value, and parse all share one ceiling. Alternatively lower the roster-file byte gate to match MAX_PARSE_CHARS (JSON import can keep the 8 MB gate).
testUpgrade: Parameterized RosterModal test over stored-input sizes {600k, 2M, 8M chars from a simulated file load, plus a 20M-char paste via onChange}: assert the value handed back to the textarea (and to parseRoster) is length <= the cap, so any future widening of MAX_FILE_BYTES or removal of the slice re-trips it. Pair with a fuzz generator that emits random-length delimiter-free and all-duplicate blobs to cover the degenerate scan.

summary: Import re-measures with uncapped O(n·(n+m)) core metrics synchronously; the density cap still admits a >1s main-thread freeze.
failure: The density gate 2·m <= BUDDY_MAX·n (BUDDY_MAX=12, MAX_IMPORT_N=2000) admits m up to 12000 at n=2000. importGraph then calls allPairsSummary(g) and girth(g) on the main thread; girth() only early-exits when best===3, so a crafted bipartite ~12-regular file (girth 4) forces the full n-source sweep. Measured on lib/dist: allPairsSummary 270 ms + girth 386 ms = ~658 ms of pure metric work (n=2000, m=12000, connected, girth 4), before JSON.parse, graph build, and rendering ~12000 <line> + ~2000 node groups — a >1 s synchronous freeze from one hostile-but-valid import. It is bounded and documented as a follow-on, but the density cap alone does not bound the O(n·(n+m)) metric cost.
remediation: Bound the metric work, not just density: either lower MAX_IMPORT_N, add a combined n·(n+m) work ceiling refused up front, or route import re-measurement through the generation worker (the documented clean follow-on). At minimum, refuse files whose (n, edge-count) product exceeds a wall-clock budget with a plain-language error.
testUpgrade: Parameterized perf test over crafted worst-case files {max-density bipartite (girth>3) at n=MAX_IMPORT_N; near-complete allowed corner; long-path high-diameter} asserting importGraph() returns under a fixed wall-clock budget (e.g. 250 ms) — so raising MAX_IMPORT_N or BUDDY_MAX without addressing metric cost fails the test. Add a fuzz generator producing random valid files up to the caps and assert no single import exceeds the budget.

summary: The min-separation knob (a girth-flavored degrees-of-separation value, core default 5) is clamped to [BUDDY_MIN, BUDDY_MAX]=[2,12] — constants named for and otherwise used as BUDDY COUNT (setK, buddies sanitize, and the density cap 2m<=BUDDY_MAX*n). Two unrelated quantities now share one bound. Same reuse at SettingsControls.tsx:43-44 (input min/max) and importGraph.ts:36 (sanitizeSettings).
failure: A maintainer raises BUDDY_MAX from 12 to 20 to allow more buddies per person -> the min-separation stepper and the import clamp silently begin accepting up to 20 degrees of separation (and the density ceiling loosens too), with no compile error and no failing test. The separation ceiling moved for a reason that has nothing to do with separation.
remediation: Introduce dedicated SEPARATION_MIN/SEPARATION_MAX in model.ts (or a core-provided bound) and use them in setMinSep, the number input min/max, and sanitizeSettings; leave BUDDY_MIN/BUDDY_MAX to buddy count and the density cap only.
testUpgrade: Parameterized test that the imported/settings minSeparation clamp is independent of BUDDY_MAX: table of declared minSeparation values (below-min, in-range, above-max) asserting clamp to SEPARATION_MIN/MAX, plus an assertion that SEPARATION_MAX !== BUDDY_MAX so a future edit to one can't silently move the other.

summary: The default seed literal 12345 is written twice — DEFAULT_SETTINGS (model.ts:14) and sanitizeSettings' fallback (importGraph.ts:37) — and both mirror the core's un-exported default seed in buildBuddyGraph. There is no single named constant tying them together.
failure: A maintainer changes the app's default seed in DEFAULT_SETTINGS but misses the importGraph fallback -> importing a hand-authored file that omits the seed field yields a GraphView whose reroll baseline (12345) differs from a freshly generated roster's default, producing a different 'Different arrangement' sequence for two rosters the user believes are configured identically. Silent, no error.
remediation: Define `export const DEFAULT_SEED = 12345;` in model.ts and reference it from both DEFAULT_SETTINGS.seed and sanitizeSettings' fallback (and consider documenting it as intentionally matching the core default).
testUpgrade: Test asserting importGraph({version:1,people,edges}) with NO settings.seed yields settings.seed === DEFAULT_SETTINGS.seed, parameterized over files with and without a settings block, so the two defaults can never drift.

summary: The stylesheet header and app/CLAUDE.md both promise 'a light theme is a later token-swap,' but several color literals hardcode the value of an existing CSS custom property instead of referencing it: --bg (#0a0e1a) is inlined as the node-label halo stroke (line 74) and the active toggle text color (line 101); --panel-solid (#0e1626) is inlined as .btn-warm text (line 90).
failure: A future light-theme change that only edits the :root tokens (exactly the promised 'token-swap') leaves these dark literals in place -> the node labels get a black halo stroke on a light background and the warm/toggle button text stays dark-on-light or vanishes, silently breaking WCAG-AA contrast that the tokens were supposed to guarantee.
remediation: Replace the token-duplicating literals with var(--bg) / var(--panel-solid) (SVG presentation properties accept CSS custom properties via the stylesheet). For the remaining one-off shades (#0b1220, #0b1322, #14203a, #08131a) that have no token, promote them to named tokens so the whole palette swaps together.
testUpgrade: A small CI guard (grep/lint test) over app.css asserting no 6-digit hex literal outside :root equals the value of any defined --token, so a color that duplicates a token must be written as var(--token).

summary: importGraph only rejects names containing comma/newline, but accepts empty, whitespace-only, and duplicate names that the roster editor's parseRoster silently drops or merges — so Edit→regenerate deletes people and shifts every downstream buddy assignment.
failure: Import a hand-authored file whose people are [{id:0,name:"Alice"},{id:1,name:"   "},{id:2,name:"Bob"}] (or a case-insensitive/exact duplicate like ["Alice","alice"]). Import succeeds and renders 3 people. Click "Edit people" (App.tsx:140 sets initialText={names.join("\n")}) then Generate: RosterModal calls onGenerate(parsed.names,...) with parseRoster's output, which trims "   "→"" and drops it (parseRoster.ts:45 `if (!token) continue`) or drops the case-insensitive duplicate (parseRoster.ts:48). Roster silently becomes 2 people; person at position 1 vanishes and positions 1..n-1 shift, so every regenerated buddy set is mislabeled. Reproduced: a parseRoster(names.join("\n")).names===names round-trip test fails on ["Alice","   ","Bob"], ["Alice","","Bob"], ["Alice","alice"], ["Alice","Alice"], and [" Alice ","Bob"]. This is the SAME class the round-6 comma/newline guard (importGraph.ts:91-93, whose own comment cites "silently split into two people on an Edit→regenerate") was added to close — the fix is incomplete.
remediation: Make the parser the single source of truth for name validity: after building `names`, reject the file when it wouldn't round-trip — e.g. `if (parseRoster(names.join("\n")).names.length !== names.length || !parseRoster(...).names.every((x,i)=>x===names[i])) throw new ImportError(...)`, or explicitly refuse empty/whitespace-only names and case-insensitive duplicates alongside the existing comma/newline check. This guarantees the displayed roster survives an Edit→regenerate unchanged.
testUpgrade: Add a parameterized round-trip invariant test (in app/test/importExport.roundtrip.test.ts or a new importGraph.test.ts) over an adversarial name table — comma, newline, "", "   ", exact dup, case-differing dup, leading/trailing spaces — asserting that importGraph EITHER throws ImportError OR yields names for which `parseRoster(view.names.join("\n")).names` deep-equals `view.names`. Strengthen it into a property/fuzz test generating random name arrays and asserting the same accept⇒round-trip-stable invariant, which also covers Unicode/whitespace variants not enumerated here. The existing importExport.roundtrip test is too narrow (it round-trips edges/metrics but never feeds imported names back through parseRoster).

summary: Neither file <input> clears e.target.value after handling, so selecting the same filename twice never re-fires onChange (same class in RosterModal.tsx:76).
failure: User clicks Import, picks graph.json, import fails (flash toast). User edits graph.json externally, clicks Import, re-picks the SAME graph.json -> the browser suppresses the change event because value is unchanged -> nothing happens, no toast, no reload. Identical in RosterModal's .txt/.csv input: re-choosing a same-named roster file after an external edit is a silent no-op.
remediation: Reset the input in the change handler after capturing the file, e.g. onChange={(e)=>{ void handleImportFile(e.target.files?.[0]); e.currentTarget.value=""; }} (and likewise in RosterModal.readFile's caller). Clearing value is safe because the File is already captured before the reset.
testUpgrade: Parameterized jsdom test over both inputs (App import + RosterModal choose-file): fire change with a File named X, then fire change again with another File also named X; assert the second selection is still processed (handler/import invoked twice) rather than silently dropped. Fuzz the filename to guard the class.

summary: Explicit polish="on" has no roster-size gate, so a modest roster runs the core polish loop (O(n·m)/iter × 20000 iters) for tens of seconds to minutes with no cancel affordance during first generation.
failure: Enter ~150 names, Advanced → Polish=on, Generate → worker runs 28.3 s (measured against lib/dist); 250 names = 79.3 s; 350 names > 120 s (unfinished). feasibility() emits no warning below n=300 (feasibility.ts:47), so 150–250 people get zero preflight notice. During the FIRST generation App renders only the uncancellable `busy` overlay (view=null, so no Edit/Cancel button per App.tsx:139/145) — only recovery is a page reload. Also reachable via import: a file with settings.polish=true survives sanitizeSettings (importGraph.ts:46) and drives the same cost on the next reroll. The core auto-caps polish at n<=120 (resolveWantPolish) for exactly this reason; the app lets the UI toggle / imported file bypass that cap.
remediation: Gate explicit polish by n in the app before dispatch (mirror the core's n<=120 auto cap: refuse/ignore polish=on above the cap, or scale polishIters with n), and/or make the first-generation overlay cancellable via the worker hook's reset() (it already swaps the worker). Make feasibility() reflect polish cost, not just n>300.
testUpgrade: Parameterized table over (n ∈ {80,150,250,400,1000}, polish ∈ {auto,on,off}) asserting the app never dispatches a GenerateRequest that requests polish when n exceeds the app's polish cap; plus a fuzz generator over Settings that includes polish=true at large n and checks the dispatched request carries a bounded-cost polish flag.

summary: "Different arrangement" (handleReroll bumps seed by 1) is a silent no-op for every roster larger than 120 people: seed only feeds the polish RNG, and polish auto-disables above n=120, so the RNG-free greedy returns byte-identical edges.
failure: buildBuddyGraph(200,4,{seed:1}) vs {seed:99999} produce identical edges (reproduced); buildBuddyGraph(100,...) differs. With default polish="auto", any roster n>120 makes handleReroll re-run generation (tens of seconds at large n), reset selection, show "Generating…", then return the exact same graph — the advertised control does nothing and wastes a multi-second regeneration. This is the dual of the determinism-integrity focus: the same roster cannot be varied even though the UI claims a new arrangement.
remediation: Either make the seed materially vary generation (lib-first: a seed-influenced deterministic tie-break so reroll varies without polish), or in the app disable/relabel "Different arrangement" when it cannot vary the result (n>120 && polish!=on), or force a polish reroll for that action — don't silently re-run and return an identical graph.
testUpgrade: Property test spanning n across the polish cap (n ∈ {60,120,121,300,800}): assert that either the reroll's seed++ changes view.edges OR the reroll control is disabled, so a future shift in the polish cap can't reintroduce a silent no-op.

summary: setSeed accepts any integer including values >= 2^53, where handleReroll's `seed + 1` is a no-op at float precision, so even in the polish-on regime reroll can return an identical graph.
failure: Type 9007199254740992 (2^53) into Seed; Number.isInteger is true so it's stored. handleReroll computes settings.seed + 1 = 2^53 (unchanged in IEEE-754), so the polish RNG seed never advances and reroll repeats the same graph. Same latent gap for an imported settings.seed (sanitizeSettings passes any integer through, importGraph.ts:45).
remediation: Clamp seed to a safe range (e.g. [0, 2^31)) in SettingsControls.setSeed and sanitizeSettings, or advance the seed with modular wraparound so seed++ always changes the value.
testUpgrade: Parameterized seeds near the boundary ({2^53-1, 2^53, 2^53+2, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER}) asserting the next-arrangement seed strictly differs from the current one after the app's advance logic.

summary: The prominent "↻ Different arrangement" reroll button silently does nothing for rosters over 120 people. It only bumps settings.seed, but the core's greedy generator is RNG-free and its auto-polish (the sole seed-dependent stage) is capped at n<=120. So for n>120 with the default polish:"auto" (or polish off), seed++ yields a byte-identical graph and no visible change or feedback.
failure: 200 people + DEFAULT_SETTINGS (polish "auto"): click "Different arrangement" -> identical edges, no change, no message. Verified against the core: buildBuddyGraph(200,4,{seed:12345}) and {seed:12346} return identical edge lists with polished:false (n=30 differs, n=121 and n=200 identical).
remediation: Thread the core's BuddyResult.polished (currently dropped in viewFromResult, model.ts:166) into GraphView. In handleReroll, when the current view was produced with polished===false, either disable the button or flash a plain-language note (mirroring the feasibility flash), e.g. "This is already the deterministic best arrangement for this size — turn on Polish in Advanced to see variations." Do not hardcode 120 in the app; drive it off the returned polished flag so it stays correct if the core's auto threshold moves.
testUpgrade: Parameterized test over n in {12, 60, 121, 300}: generate with seed S and S+1; assert edges differ iff the returned BuddyResult.polished is true (guards the class: reroll variability must track the seed-dependent stage, not an assumed 'seed always rerolls').

summary: The "Known follow-ons" note states import size caps are "(`MAX_IMPORT_N`=2000 etc.) ... tighter than generation's". After the round-6 change MAX_IMPORT_N = MAX_ROSTER_N = 1000 (importGraph.ts:29, model.ts:34), so the cited value (2000) is wrong and the relationship is inverted: the import cap now EQUALS the generation ceiling, not tighter — importGraph.ts:26-30 explicitly documents that equality. A new contributor reading the working-notes doc for context is misled about both the number and the design rationale.
failure: Contributor reads app/CLAUDE.md to size a new import path -> believes import is capped at 2000 and is intentionally stricter than generation -> reasons/changes code against a cap that is actually 1000 and equal, contradicting importGraph.ts's own comment.
remediation: Update the note to: "its size caps (`MAX_IMPORT_N` = `MAX_ROSTER_N` = 1000) match generation's ceiling (a re-rollable import shouldn't display more than the app can generate); lifting this means routing import through the worker." Prefer referencing the constant name over a literal so the doc can't drift on the next change.
testUpgrade: Add a docs-consistency test (extend cssTokens.test.ts pattern) that greps app/CLAUDE.md for a hardcoded MAX_IMPORT_N=<number> and asserts it equals the imported MAX_IMPORT_N value, failing when the doc literal and the constant diverge.

summary: app/_g.mjs is a committed one-off benchmark scratch file that hardcodes an absolute machine path (`import { buildBuddyGraph } from "/home/user/ringweave/lib/dist/core/index.js"`). It is git-tracked, referenced by no package.json script, excluded from no gitignore, and cannot run on any other machine. It sits at the app package root where a contributor will trip over it and either try (and fail) to run it or mistake it for part of the app.
failure: On any clone not at /home/user/ringweave, `node app/_g.mjs` throws ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND; the file also survives review as unexplained dead code with a non-portable path.
remediation: Delete app/_g.mjs. If a generation benchmark is worth keeping, move it under a scripts/ or bench/ dir, import via the package specifier ("ringweave") not an absolute path, and wire it to an npm script so it stays runnable and discoverable.
testUpgrade: Add a repo-hygiene test that asserts no tracked source file outside node_modules/dist contains an absolute filesystem path literal (e.g. matches /\"\/home\//), guarding against machine-specific paths being committed again.

summary: rerollWouldVary predicts variation from the polish-enabled axis only, so "Different arrangement" silently regenerates a byte-identical graph (no explanatory flash) for common small rosters where the graph is uniquely determined / polish converges identically.
failure: Default settings (buddies=4, polish "auto", seed 12345). Roster of 6, 8, 10, or 12 people. Click "↻ Different arrangement" (App.handleReroll bumps seed 12345->12346). rerollWouldVary(n,{polish:"auto"}) returns true (n<=120 && polish!==false), so the gate does NOT flash — it calls bg.generate. Verified: buildBuddyGraph(6|8|10|12, 4, {seed:12345}) and {seed:12346} return byte-identical edges (polished=true). Ring positions depend only on n and edges are identical, so the user sees no change and no message — exactly the silent no-op the round-7 fix declared it eliminated. Probe over n=3..24,k=4 shows 12/12 seed bumps identical for n=3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,12.
remediation: rerollWouldVary cannot predict this pre-hoc without running generation. Move the "explain, don't silently no-op" decision to AFTER the worker returns: in useBuddyGraph, compare the new result's edges to the current view's edges and, when identical, surface the "already the best arrangement" notice (and keep the current graph) instead of swapping in an indistinguishable view. Keep the existing pre-hoc gate for the polish-off / n>POLISH_MAX_N axis as a cheap fast-path, but add the post-generation identical-edges check to cover the uniquely-determined / polish-converged case.
testUpgrade: Class: seed-bump reroll must either change the edges or surface the explanatory notice — never a silent identical regeneration. Replace reroll.test's single n=30 case with a table-driven / property test over n in [3, POLISH_MAX_N] and k in [2, min(BUDDY_MAX, n-1)] under default settings asserting: for each (n,k), buildBuddyGraph(n,k,{seed}) vs {seed:seed+1} — if edges are identical then the app path must flash the notice (assert via a useBuddyGraph/handleReroll-level test that identical results produce a user-visible "already the best" message), i.e. no (n,k,seed) yields an edges-identical regeneration with an empty notice. The current n=30 case is too narrow — 30 happens to vary — so it never exercised the common 5–12 person sizes.

summary: Reroll block message tells the user to 'turn on Polish' even when Polish is already ON and the group is too large for polish to ever run.
failure: Enter 121+ names, set Polish=on in Advanced, Generate, then click 'Different arrangement'. handleReroll computes rerollWouldVary(121,{polish:true}) => false (121<=120 is false) and flashes 'This is already the best arrangement for a group this size - turn on Polish (Advanced) for small groups to vary it.' The advice is contradictory: polish is already on, and the app deliberately downgrades polish->auto above POLISH_MAX_N so no seed can ever vary a 121-person graph. The 'turn on Polish' guidance is also wrong for the polish=auto/large-n case, since polish cannot run above 120 in this app at all.
remediation: Branch the flash reason on (n, settings.polish): when n>POLISH_MAX_N, say the group is too large for a different arrangement (polish only varies small groups) - do not suggest enabling something already enabled or that the app suppresses. Reserve the 'turn on Polish' hint for the n<=POLISH_MAX_N && polish===false case.
testUpgrade: Extract a pure rerollBlockReason(n, settings) and parameterize over polish in {off, auto, on} x n in {small, >POLISH_MAX_N}: assert the too-large branches never contain the string 'turn on Polish' when settings.polish is already true, and that the 'turn on Polish' hint appears only when polish===false && n<=POLISH_MAX_N.

summary: A valid import whose names total more than MAX_PARSE_CHARS (500k) is refused with a message blaming commas/line-breaks/uniqueness, none of which is the real cause.
failure: Import a version-1 file with, e.g., 900 people (<=MAX_IMPORT_N) whose names are each ~600 chars and all valid (non-empty, unique, no commas/newlines). names.join('\n') exceeds MAX_PARSE_CHARS, so parseRoster truncates and drops trailing names; roundTrip.length < n triggers ImportError('Every name must be non-empty, unique (case-insensitively), and free of commas or line breaks.') even though every name satisfies all of those.
remediation: Detect the truncation case (raw join length > MAX_PARSE_CHARS, or parseRoster surfacing its truncation warning) and emit a length-specific message; or size-check total name length up front with its own reason rather than letting the round-trip check speak for it.
testUpgrade: Fuzz importGraph with n names of randomized length where sum(length)+n exceeds MAX_PARSE_CHARS but each name is individually valid: assert the file is either accepted and round-trips, or refused with a message that mentions size/length - never the commas/line-breaks message.

summary: rerollWouldVary gates only on whether polish RUNS, not whether it actually varies the graph, so 'Different arrangement' is a silent no-op for small rosters where the optimal graph is unique.
failure: Enter 5 names, keep the default 4 buddies (n=5,k=4 -> K5, the unique graph). rerollWouldVary(5,{polish:'auto'}) returns true, so handleReroll (App.tsx:60) proceeds to bg.generate; the worker returns byte-identical edges (verified: buildBuddyGraph(n,k,seed) is identical across seeds 1/2/99999 for every n<=12 at k=4, and for every complete graph n=k+1). The graph does not change and NO explanatory flash fires. This is the exact silent no-op the round-7 fix claimed to eliminate; its docstring even says 'the UI explains instead of silently doing nothing.' The n>POLISH_MAX_N branch is handled but the small-n plateau is not.
remediation: rerollWouldVary is necessary but not sufficient. Detect the identical-result case for real rather than by a polish-runs heuristic: after a reroll's generation completes, compare the new result's edges to the current view's edges and, if unchanged, flash the 'already the best arrangement for a group this size' notice instead of swapping in an identical view. (A cheap partial guard is to also treat n<=k+1 / complete graphs as non-varying, but the robust fix is the post-hoc edge comparison, since the plateau extends past n=k+1 — n=12,k=4 is also invariant.)
testUpgrade: Parameterize reroll.test.ts over n in {5,6,7,8,10,12,15,20,30} at k=4: for every n where the UI would proceed with a reroll, assert buildBuddyGraph(n,k,{seed:1}).edges differs from {seed:2}.edges — OR that the reroll path surfaces the explanatory flash. The current test only checks n=30 (which varies) and n>cap (which is gated), so it misses the whole small-n identical-output band.

summary: The reroll explanatory flash tells the user to 'turn on Polish' even when polish is already explicitly ON, because at n>POLISH_MAX_N the real blocker is size, not the polish setting.
failure: Set Polish=on in Advanced, generate a 200-person roster, click 'Different arrangement'. feasibility passes; rerollWouldVary(200,{polish:true}) is false (200>120), so it flashes 'This is already the best arrangement for a group this size — turn on Polish (Advanced) for small groups to vary it.' Polish is already on, and turning it on cannot help at this size (generate() downgrades polish=true to 'auto' above POLISH_MAX_N anyway), so the advice is contradictory and unactionable.
remediation: Branch the message on why it won't vary: when settings.polish!==false and n>POLISH_MAX_N, say the group is too large for the seed-dependent polish stage (so rerolling can't change it), rather than advising to enable polish. Only suggest enabling polish when polish===false and n<=POLISH_MAX_N.
testUpgrade: Add a unit test that, for (polish:true, n>POLISH_MAX_N), the reroll-blocked message does NOT contain 'turn on Polish', and for (polish:false, n<=POLISH_MAX_N) it DOES — parameterizing the message-selection logic (extract it from the inline handler so it is testable).

summary: finiteOrNull is exported but only referenced inside model.ts (girth normalization at line 142) and no test uses it, widening the module's public surface for no consumer.
failure: grep across app/src and app/test shows finiteOrNull's only reference is model.ts:142. An exported symbol reads as 'part of the model API' to a future contributor and invites divergent second uses; it is internal-only today.
remediation: Drop the `export` on finiteOrNull (make it a module-local helper), or if it is meant to pair with the exported degreeExtent/quality as reusable model utilities, add a one-line note saying so and cover it in quality.test.ts. Prefer removing the export.
testUpgrade: Extend hygiene.test.ts (or a new exports test) to flag exported functions in model.ts that have zero references outside their defining file, guarding the unused-public-surface class.

summary: For an explicit polish=on roster above POLISH_MAX_N (which useBuddyGraph silently downgrades to "auto"), the reroll gate flashes "turn on Polish (Advanced) for small groups to vary it" even though the user already has polish on.
failure: Settings polish=true (user-selected), roster of 200 people. useBuddyGraph.generate downgrades polish true->"auto" for n>POLISH_MAX_N (so the graph is never polished), and rerollWouldVary(200,{polish:true}) returns false (n<=120 fails), so handleReroll flashes a message telling the user to enable Polish — which they already enabled. The advice is inapplicable at this size and contradicts the user's current setting.
remediation: Tailor the flash by branch: when n>POLISH_MAX_N, say polish is unavailable/disabled for groups this large (the seed-free greedy is already optimal for the size) rather than advising to enable it; reserve the "turn on Polish" copy for the n<=POLISH_MAX_N && polish===false branch where it is actionable.
testUpgrade: Parameterize a handleReroll-message test over the {polish: false|"auto"|true} x {n<=POLISH_MAX_N, n>POLISH_MAX_N} matrix, asserting the flashed copy matches the actionable branch (only the polish-off, small-n cell mentions enabling Polish; the large-n cells do not advise enabling something the app force-disables).

summary: toCsv quotes fields but does not neutralize leading =,+,-,@; an imported/shared roster name becomes an executable formula when the exported buddies.csv is opened in a spreadsheet.
failure: Import a shared BuddyGraph JSON containing a person named '=HYPERLINK("http://x","click")' (or '-2+3', '@SUM(...)'). BuddyList 'CSV' export writes it verbatim inside quotes; Excel/Sheets interpret the leading = and evaluate the formula on open. Same for copyAll's plain-text output pasted into a sheet.
remediation: Prefix any cell beginning with =,+,-,@ (or tab/CR) with a leading apostrophe or space in toCsv before quoting, neutralizing formula evaluation while preserving the text on re-import.
testUpgrade: Property test toCsv over cells beginning with each of = + - @ and a control set: assert each emitted field, when parsed back, yields the original text and that no field passed to a spreadsheet would begin with a formula trigger.

summary: The identical-regeneration callback always says "That's already the best arrangement for a group this size," but it fires on ANY same-roster re-generation (including an Edit→Generate with no change) and overclaims optimality when quality<1.
failure: With roster [A..E] and the same settings, open "Edit people" and click Generate without changing anything (or reroll a small polish-converged but sub-optimal graph): the worker returns byte-identical edges, so useBuddyGraph fires onIdenticalReroll and App flashes "already the best arrangement for a group this size" — attributing an unchanged-input / polish-plateau no-op to group SIZE, and asserting "best" even when QualityPanel shows <100%.
remediation: Make the copy cause-agnostic and non-overclaiming, e.g. "That arrangement didn't change — this is the layout the current settings produce." Optionally only wire onIdenticalReroll for the reroll action (pass an intent flag through generate) so an Edit→Generate no-op doesn't read as a failed reroll.
testUpgrade: Class: message-vs-reality for no-op regenerations. Add a parameterized useBuddyGraph.test.tsx case table over {trigger: reroll | edit-regenerate} × {graph optimal | sub-optimal} asserting the notified copy never claims size as the cause for a sub-optimal graph and never says "best" when metrics.quality<1; widen it to also cover the edit-regenerate-identical path, which the current single K5 reroll test doesn't exercise.

summary: handleReroll computes seed+1 and persists it via setSettings without re-clamping to [0, SEED_MAX], violating the clamp invariant documented in model.ts:43-45.
failure: Repeatedly clicking "Different arrangement" drives settings.seed monotonically past SEED_MAX (2^31-1) and, over an astronomically large number of rerolls, past 2^53 where seed+1 no longer advances at float precision (and, if the core RNG masks to 32 bits, seeds beyond 2^31 could alias earlier seeds, silently turning a reroll into a no-op). Not reachably harmful in practice (would require ~2^31 rerolls), so present-day risk is nil; it is an integrity/consistency gap against the stated invariant.
remediation: Clamp the reroll seed the same way inputs are clamped, e.g. seed: settings.seed >= SEED_MAX ? 0 : settings.seed + 1 (wrap within [0, SEED_MAX]), so the dispatched/stored seed always honors the model.ts contract.
testUpgrade: Add a parameterized reroll test over boundary seeds {0, SEED_MAX-1, SEED_MAX, SEED_MAX+5} asserting the seed passed to generate stays an integer within [0, SEED_MAX] and that consecutive rerolls always produce distinct seed values (guarding the class of seed-domain-overflow, not just the one boundary).

summary: The post-hoc identical-reroll callback fires for ANY byte-identical regeneration, but its copy asserts optimality ("already the best arrangement") and also misfires on a plain re-Generate that was never a reroll request.
failure: Two concrete paths through the ONE shared no-op detector in useBuddyGraph (effect at useBuddyGraph.ts:49). (1) Open "Edit people" and click Generate without changing anything (same roster, same seed): handleGenerate -> bg.generate -> worker returns identical edges -> sameStrings&&sameEdges true -> onIdenticalReroll fires -> flash "That's already the best arrangement for a group this size" even though the user never asked for a different arrangement. (2) Any small graph that polish-converges to the same LOCAL optimum across seeds but scores < 100% on the Moore gauge (QualityPanel shows q<100) will, on "Different arrangement", flash "already the best arrangement" — directly contradicting the sub-100% gauge, because the code establishes convergence/identity, not optimality.
remediation: Separate the signal from the claim. In useBuddyGraph, keep onIdenticalReroll as a pure "identical result" event. In App, gate the wording on intent and on the gauge: only reroll (not modal Generate) should surface it, and phrase it as "couldn't find a different arrangement" rather than "the best arrangement" unless view.metrics.quality === 1. E.g. pass a boolean to distinguish reroll-triggered generations, and branch the copy on quality===1.
testUpgrade: Parameterize the useBuddyGraph test over trigger source {reroll, fresh-generate} x {identical edges, quality<1 vs quality==1}: assert onIdenticalReroll fires whenever edges are byte-identical (documenting the shared codepath) AND add a model/App-level assertion that the optimality wording is only emitted when metrics.quality===1, so copy can never contradict the gauge.

summary: One callback has two names within a single 85-line file: the parameter/doc call it `onIdenticalReroll`, but the ref that actually invokes it is `onNoop`.
failure: A maintainer reading the effect body sees `onNoop.current?.()` at line 50 and must mentally re-map it back to the `onIdenticalReroll` parameter (line 27) and the JSDoc (lines 22-25) to understand what fires. `onNoop` also describes the mechanism (a no-op happened) rather than the event (an identical reroll), which is the naming smell called out in the core vocabulary lens.
remediation: Rename the ref to `onIdenticalRerollRef` (or `identicalRerollCb`) so the parameter, JSDoc, and call site all use one what-name. Purely mechanical.
testUpgrade: N/A (naming); a lint rule forbidding ref-vs-param name divergence for the same callback would guard the class, but this is not test-guardable behavior.

summary: The round-8 CSV formula neutralization is applied to the CSV export but not to the sibling clipboard-copy path, which emits the same untrusted roster names into the same spreadsheet-paste sink.
failure: Import (or hand-edit) a file whose person name is `=HYPERLINK("http://evil","click")` (a valid non-empty, unique, comma/newline-free name that passes importGraph's round-trip). Click CSV -> the cell is neutralized to `"'=HYPERLINK(...)"` (safe). Click Copy instead -> copyAll builds the line `=HYPERLINK("http://evil","click"): Bob, Cara` verbatim (BuddyList.tsx:17-19) and writes it as text/plain via copyText (download.ts:24). Pasting that into Excel/Sheets, where a pasted cell whose first char is `=`/`+`/`-`/`@` is parsed as a formula, reintroduces exactly the injection the CSV path was hardened against.
remediation: Lift neutralizeFormula into a shared exported helper (e.g. neutralizeCell) in download.ts and apply it on the clipboard path too — neutralize the leading name of each copyAll line the same way toCsv does — so both spreadsheet-bound sinks share one sanitizer. If clipboard is deemed out of scope, note that explicitly rather than leaving the two sinks silently divergent. Cost is low (extract one helper, add one call site); benefit closes a same-class injection vector and prevents drift as names flow to more export surfaces.
testUpgrade: Parameterize download.test.ts over the full dangerous leading-char set ['=', '+', '-', '@', '\t', '\r']: for each char c, assert BOTH the CSV serializer AND the clipboard-text builder neutralize a name c+'cmd', driven from a single shared neutralizeCell so a future sink that forgets to call it fails the class test, not just the one input.

summary: CSV formula-injection neutralization guards only the CSV export path (toCsv/neutralizeFormula); the parallel "Copy" clipboard path emits the same untrusted names with no neutralization, so the mitigation is asymmetric and a maintainer can't tell whether the omission is intentional.
failure: Import a file whose person name is `=HYPERLINK("http://evil","x")`. Clicking "CSV" produces `"'=HYPERLINK..."` (neutralized). Clicking "Copy" (copyAll, lines 16-25) writes `=HYPERLINK("http://evil","x"): Bob, Cara` to the clipboard with the leading `=` intact. Exploitability is reduced by the `: buddies` suffix (it often makes the formula a syntax error when pasted into a single cell), but the two paths share a threat model yet only one is hardened — a defense-in-depth inconsistency that reads as a bug or an oversight.
remediation: Route both exports through one neutralizer. Extract neutralizeFormula (or a `safeCell`) and apply it per line in copyAll as well, or document at the copyAll call site why the clipboard path is exempt if that is a deliberate decision.
testUpgrade: Add a parameterized test over the dangerous leading set [=,+,-,@,\t,\r] asserting BOTH the CSV cell AND the clipboard line for a hostile name are neutralized (prefixed with an apostrophe / rendered inert), so future export surfaces inherit the guarantee as a class.

summary: The clipboard Copy path's leading-char-only neutralizeCell guard is defeated by a TAB or CR embedded inside an imported name, re-opening the exact spreadsheet formula-injection the round-9 fix claimed to close (breaking the stated CSV/Copy parity).
failure: Import a file whose person name is "foo\t=cmd(1)" (passes importGraph: parseRoster's /[^\n,]+/ tokenizer keeps internal \t/\r, so the round-trip check accepts it). Click Copy -> clipboard line is `foo\t=cmd(1): Bob, Cara`. Paste into Excel/Sheets (tab-delimited paste is the default): it splits into cell `foo` and cell `=cmd(1): Bob, Cara`, the second being a live formula. `foo\r=cmd(1)` starts a new ROW beginning with the formula. neutralizeCell only tests the first char (/^[=+\-@\t\r]/), so the embedded delimiter is never guarded. CSV export is NOT affected (RFC-4180 quoting contains the tab), so the two sinks the commit says now share one guard are still asymmetric. Reproduced via a script.
remediation: Make names free of control characters the authority the same way commas/newlines already are: reject any name containing a control char (e.g. /[�-]/, notably \t and \r) in importGraph's name-integrity check (and parseRoster), so a cell/row-splitting delimiter can never enter a name. Alternatively (or additionally), have the copy/CSV serializers strip or escape embedded \t/\r rather than only prefixing on the leading char. Prefer the import-side refusal since it also protects any future paste sink.
testUpgrade: Class = 'a spreadsheet-bound sink must neutralize EVERY would-be-cell, not just the leading char.' Parameterize download.test.ts / buddyListCopy.test.tsx over a table of hostile names that place a formula char after an embedded delimiter ("foo\t=cmd", "foo\r-2+3", "foo\t@SUM(A1)") and assert: splitting the produced Copy line on /[\t\r]/ yields NO field matching /^[=+\-@]/. Add an importGraph.roundtrip test asserting a name containing \t or \r is refused (widen the existing round-trip generator, which today only fuzzes commas/newlines/dupes, to include control chars). The current download.test.ts loop tests \t/\r only as leading chars, so it cannot catch this.

summary: model.ts advertises itself as the single source that keeps the two Settings producers from diverging, but the minSeparation DEFAULT is not centralized there: SettingsControls falls back to the core's DEFAULT_MIN_SEPARATION (5) while importGraph's sanitizeSettings falls back to SEPARATION_MIN (2) for an invalid value, so the two producers of a Settings.minSeparation disagree.
failure: Import a file with settings.minSeparation:3.5 (non-integer): sanitizeInt(3.5,2,12,2) is not an integer so it returns the fallback 2, and v.settings.minSeparation becomes 2. A freshly configured graph (DEFAULT_SETTINGS has no minSeparation) instead surfaces DEFAULT_MIN_SEPARATION=5 via `settings.minSeparation ?? DEFAULT_MIN_SEPARATION` in SettingsControls.tsx:45. So the app's notion of the default min-separation is 5 in the fresh path and 2 after an invalid import, and a later reroll of that import then generates with mind=2 instead of the intended 5. SettingsControls.tsx:1 is also the only UI panel that reaches past model.ts directly into a core export (DEFAULT_MIN_SEPARATION), the exact coupling model.ts's single-source comment is meant to prevent.
remediation: Centralize the separation default in model.ts (e.g. export SEPARATION_DEFAULT, re-exporting or mirroring the core's DEFAULT_MIN_SEPARATION with a sync note like the other range constants), and use that single constant as the fallback in BOTH sanitizeSettings (importGraph.ts:45) and setMinSep / the display default (SettingsControls.tsx:21,45). SettingsControls should import the default from model.ts, not from ringweave.
testUpgrade: Parameterized test over every Settings field: for each field, importGraph({...,settings:{[field]: <invalid value>}}).settings[field] must equal the canonical default model/UI surfaces for an UNSET field. Concretely assert importGraph(...,{minSeparation:2.5}).settings.minSeparation === SEPARATION_DEFAULT === (SettingsControls' unset display value), so the two producers can never fall back to different values again.
