summary: POLISH_MAX_N=120 hand-duplicates the core's polish auto-cap, which is an un-exported literal in resolveWantPolish (lib/src/core/index.ts:310); nothing keeps them in sync.
failure: Raise the core's auto-cap above 120 (e.g. to 200 in lib resolveWantPolish). useBuddyGraph.generate (useBuddyGraph.ts:66-67) still downgrades an explicit polish=true to "auto" only when names.length > POLISH_MAX_N(120); but at n=150 the core's "auto" now ENABLES polish, so the guard's comment ('Downgrade to auto, which the core disables at this size anyway') is false and a hostile imported polish=true at n in (120, coreCap] runs the exact O(n·m) polish the guard exists to suppress. No app test catches it because reroll.test/useBuddyGraph.test import the app's own POLISH_MAX_N, not the core's behavior.
remediation: Export the cap from the core (e.g. `export const AUTO_POLISH_MAX_N = 120` used by resolveWantPolish) and set `POLISH_MAX_N = AUTO_POLISH_MAX_N` in model.ts, so the app can't drift. If a lib change is undesirable now, add a boundary test that pins the app constant to real core behavior.
testUpgrade: Parameterized test over n in {POLISH_MAX_N-1, POLISH_MAX_N, POLISH_MAX_N+1} asserting buildBuddyGraph(n,4,{polish:'auto'}).polished flips from true to false exactly at POLISH_MAX_N — a core cap change then fails app CI instead of silently desyncing.

summary: The buddy-label projection `buddyNames(view,i).join(", ") || "—"` is copy-pasted identically in BuddyList.tsx:53 and Slips.tsx:12.
failure: A contributor changes the empty-buddy glyph or separator (e.g. from '—' to 'no buddies yet', or ', ' to ' · ') in BuddyList but not Slips, so the on-screen list and the printed slips silently disagree for the same person — a display inconsistency with no compile error to flag it.
remediation: Add `export function buddyLabel(view: GraphView, i: number): string { return buddyNames(view, i).join(", ") || "—"; }` to model.ts (beside buddyNames) and call it from both BuddyList row and Slips card.
testUpgrade: Test with a roster containing an isolated (0-buddy) person asserting BuddyList row text === Slips card text === buddyLabel(view,i) for every i, so the two sinks are pinned to one projection.

summary: Reroll orchestration is split: useBuddyGraph owns the reroll INTENT flag, worker dispatch, and post-hoc identical-edges detection, but the pre-hoc reroll POLICY (advance seed via nextRerollSeed, feasibility() gate, rerollBlockReason() gate, resetSelection) lives inline in App.handleReroll. A second reroll trigger (the code already anticipates one: App.tsx:46 comments about a 'keyboard reroll') would have to duplicate this five-step gating sequence.
failure: Adding a keyboard-shortcut reroll (or a reroll button in another panel) forces a copy of the seed-advance + feasibility + rerollBlockReason + resetSelection + generate({reroll:true}) sequence, or a refactor at that time; the reroll contract is not encapsulated in one reusable unit despite the hook already being the home of reroll intent and detection.
remediation: Hoist the reroll policy into useBuddyGraph (or a small useReroll wrapper) as a `reroll(names, settings)` that returns a block-reason or dispatches — so all reroll entry points share one gate. Keep only the notice wording in App. Low priority: there is exactly one caller today, so this is a latent DRY/SRP concern, not a live defect.
testUpgrade: When the policy is extracted, add a test that drives reroll(names, settings) through the too-large, polish-off, and infeasible-k branches and asserts it both blocks with the right message AND never dispatches to the worker in those cases — guarding the gate as a unit independent of App.

summary: parseRoster emits the "Kept the first 1000 names — that's the maximum" warning even when the token past the cap was a duplicate (nothing was actually lost), because the cap is checked at loop top before duplicate filtering.
failure: Paste 1000 unique names followed by a duplicate of name #1: the loop fills names to 1000 on the uniques, then the 1001st token hits `names.length >= MAX_NAMES` and sets capped=true/breaks before it is recognized as a duplicate. The user has all 1000 of their distinct names yet is told the roster was truncated to a maximum, and that trailing duplicate is also not counted in the `extras` de-dupe warning. No wrong graph is produced — only a misleading warning.
remediation: Only warn about truncation when a token that would have been KEPT (a new, non-blank, non-duplicate name) was actually dropped by the cap. E.g. continue scanning past the cap counting genuinely-new names and set `capped` only if that count > 0, or peek/normalize the token and skip the cap break for duplicates/blanks.
testUpgrade: Add a table-driven parseRoster test over the cap boundary that asserts BOTH the kept count and the presence/absence of the truncation warning across classes: (a) exactly MAX_NAMES uniques -> no cap warning; (b) MAX_NAMES uniques + trailing duplicate(s) -> no cap warning (this case); (c) MAX_NAMES uniques + trailing NEW name -> cap warning present. Parameterize on the trailing-token kind (new/duplicate/blank) so the class is guarded, not just this input.

summary: forceLayout settles 300 d3-force ticks synchronously and freezes the main thread ~1.5s at the app's own n=1000 ceiling; its caps never fire for any in-range input.
failure: Import a valid n=1000 file (e.g. the sparse ring from the passing import test importExport.roundtrip.test.ts:79) or generate a ~1000-person roster -> GraphCanvas.tsx:58 computes forcePos = useMemo(() => forceLayout(n, edges)) unconditionally on the main thread during render (even while layout is 'ring'), and each reroll recomputes it. Reproduced: forceLayout(1000, ring-edges) = 1467ms; forceLayout(1000, []) = 1522ms, so cost is node-driven and FORCE_MAX_EDGES=4000 is irrelevant. FORCE_MAX_N=1000 equals MAX_IMPORT_N/MAX_ROSTER_N, so the n>FORCE_MAX_N ring fallback is dead code for real inputs and the largest allowed graph always settles synchronously.
remediation: Make the guard track wall-clock, not count: lower FORCE_MAX_N to where a synchronous 300-tick settle stays under budget (~250-300 nodes) and/or scale iters down as n grows; only compute forcePos when layout==='force' (defer the cost, and derive computeFit from ring-only or make it lazy too since GraphCanvas.tsx:59 currently reads both layouts). Robust fix: run the settle off the main thread.
testUpgrade: Class = 'in-range force settle must not freeze the main thread'. Add a parameterized time-budget test over forceLayout at n in {250,500,FORCE_MAX_N} crossed with edges in {0, n, FORCE_MAX_EDGES}, asserting each synchronous call completes under a fixed budget (e.g. 150ms), plus the invariant 'for every n<=FORCE_MAX_N the settle is within budget'. The current layout.determinism.test.ts only asserts the fallback fires ABOVE the caps (n=1001, >4000 edges) and never exercises the expensive in-range corner.

summary: copyAll re-inlines the buddy-name join instead of reusing buddyLabel, contradicting buddyLabel's "the one buddy-cell projection" comment and diverging on the empty case.
failure: Import a graph with an isolated person (e.g. {version:1, people:[P0..P3], edges:[[0,1],[1,2],[2,0]]}). The on-screen list and slips render 'P3 —' (buddyLabel), but Copy writes the line 'P3: ' (empty after the colon) because copyAll uses buddyNames(view,i).join(", ") with no em-dash fallback. A future maintainer changing buddyLabel's separator or empty glyph updates the list+slips but silently not the clipboard copy, which the buddyLabelParity test does not cover.
remediation: Give copy/CSV their sink-specific separators from a shared helper, e.g. add `buddyCell(view, i, sep = ", ")` returning `buddyNames(view,i).join(sep) || "—"` and have buddyLabel, copyAll, and exportCsv all call it (exportCsv passing "; "), so the empty glyph and default separator live in one place.
testUpgrade: Extend buddyListCopy.test.tsx into a parameterized case over rosters that include a 0-buddy person and a normal person: assert each copied line's post-colon segment equals the shared projection used by buddyLabel (same separator AND same empty representation), so a divergence in either fails.

summary: sanitizeSettings comment cites a "degree-1999 fallback" that cannot occur under the current MAX_IMPORT_N=1000 cap (max reachable degreeMax is 999).
failure: The comment describes the untrusted-value the clamp guards against as "a star graph's degree-1999 fallback"; but importGraph refuses people.length > MAX_IMPORT_N (=MAX_ROSTER_N=1000), so a star's central-node degree — the value passed as fallbackBuddies — tops out at 999. The 1999 figure implies an n=2000 ceiling that no longer exists, so a reader reasoning about the real bound is misled.
remediation: Update the number to the reachable bound (e.g. "a star import's degree-999 fallback") or drop the specific figure and say "a star import's near-n degree fallback", so the example tracks MAX_IMPORT_N instead of hardcoding a stale ceiling.
testUpgrade: Add a parameterized sanitizeSettings/importGraph test over star-shaped imports at degreeMax values up to MAX_IMPORT_N-1 (e.g. 12, 100, 999) asserting the resolved settings.buddies is always clamped into [BUDDY_MIN, BUDDY_MAX]; this pins the real reachable fallback range the comment should describe.

summary: Test fixture builds a real auto-polished graph (buildBuddyGraph(60,4) ~4.2s) under vitest's default 5000ms timeout, so the suite is non-deterministically red — the "force mode computes it" test timed out on a full `npm test` run, though it passes in isolation.
failure: Run `npm test` (full suite) on a loaded box: test/graphCanvasDefer.test.tsx:42 "force mode computes it" -> "Error: Test timed out in 5000ms." (1 failed | 98 passed). Root cause: buildBuddyGraph(n=60,k=4) auto-polish measured 4196ms (n=30=1077ms, n=24=738ms); with the 4.2s baseline + full-suite CPU contention it crosses the 5000ms default, and there is no explicit testTimeout in vitest config. The test only asserts forceLayout IS/ISN'T called, so polish is entirely irrelevant to what it verifies.
remediation: Pass polish:false to the fixtures that don't exercise polish. In graphCanvasDefer.test.tsx line 21 change to `buildBuddyGraph(n, 4, { seed: 1, polish: false })` (drops the build from ~4.2s to ~7ms). Apply the same to the other layout/render/roundtrip fixtures that only need edges/adjacency (layout.determinism.test.ts:6, graphCanvas.smoke, importExport.roundtrip.ts:261). For the few tests that MUST exercise auto-polish (quality.test.ts, reroll.test.ts already use polishIters:1), either keep polishIters small or set an explicit generous testTimeout so their cost is not gated by an unrelated default.
testUpgrade: Class = "expensive-real-generation under an implicit per-test timeout". Durable guard: (a) add a global `test.timeout`/`testTimeout` in vitest.config so no test silently rides the 5000ms default while calling into the core; and (b) add a table-driven fixture helper (e.g. `genFixture(n,k,{polish})`) used by all app tests that defaults to polish:false, so a future test author can't reintroduce a multi-second auto-polish build in a render/layout test. A CI assertion that the whole app suite finishes under a wall-clock budget would catch the regression class (the current suite is ~21s of test time, dominated by these auto-polish fixtures).

summary: The 'which positions for the current layout mode' decision is expressed independently in four places instead of one resolver: the forcePos memo (line 62), the fit memo's ring-vs-force branch (line 63), the render `target` (line 65), and the animation `to` inside the effect (line 84). All four must stay in sync.
failure: Landing the named next-milestone F8 focus/ego layout: a dev extends LayoutMode with 'focus' and adds a focusPos computation. To be correct they must edit all four sites consistently. Miss one -- e.g. compute target = focusPos but leave the effect's `to` = `forcePos ?? ringPos` (line 84) -- and the animation destination diverges from the rendered frame: nodes render at focus coordinates while the cubic-ease tween drives display toward ring/force coordinates, producing a visibly wrong settle. Miss the fit branch (line 63) and the focus layout is framed to the ring's bounding box, clipping nodes. Nothing structurally prevents the desync; it is four separate ternaries keyed on the same variable.
remediation: Introduce one positionsFor(mode): Pt[] (or a Record<LayoutMode, Pt[] | null>) computed once and consumed by fit, target, and the effect. A new mode then adds exactly one entry and cannot desync render vs. animation vs. fit -- a genuine >=2-variant seam (ring/force today, focus next), so a lookup is warranted rather than over-engineering. Low cost (~10 lines); removes a four-way sync hazard on the path of the next planned feature.
testUpgrade: Parameterized test over all LayoutMode values asserting the invariant that the positions used to render (target) are identical to the animation destination (to) and are the array fit was computed from, for each mode -- so adding a mode that desyncs any of the three fails the test rather than shipping a broken tween.

summary: RosterModal.capText pre-truncates every stored string to EXACTLY MAX_PARSE_CHARS before parseRoster runs, so parseRoster's char-truncation warning (guarded by `text.length > MAX_PARSE_CHARS`, a strict >) can never fire on the UI path. Confirmed dead: the warning is exercised only by a direct parseRoster unit test (parseRoster.test.ts:75), never through the component.
failure: Drop/paste ~2MB of names whose distinct count stays under MAX_NAMES (1000) -- e.g. long or duplicate-heavy names. capText slices to 500000 chars; parseRoster sees length == 500000, `> 500000` is false, so no 'only the first N characters were read' warning; and the name cap (1000) is never reached either, so no 'Kept the first 1000 names' warning fires. Result: the roster is silently truncated with zero user-facing notice -- the exact class of silent-truncation the parseRoster warning was written to prevent.
remediation: Either have capText surface its own truncation notice, or (simpler) don't pre-truncate to exactly the limit and let parseRoster be the single truncation authority that both bounds work and reports it, keeping one source of the '> limit' decision. Low cost; the common over-limit case is already covered by the name-cap warning, so this only closes a narrow silent-truncation gap in the specifically-touched parse area.
testUpgrade: Parameterized RosterModal test feeding over-limit inputs in two shapes -- (a) >1000 distinct names, (b) <1000 distinct but >MAX_PARSE_CHARS via few long names -- asserting a truncation warning is shown in BOTH cases (guards the class where the name cap masks the char cap).

summary: buddyNames' doc-comment claims it is 'Shared by BuddyList and Slips', but after the round-11 unification neither component uses it — both route through buddyLabel; buddyNames is now a private helper called only by buddyLabel yet is still exported.
failure: grep for `buddyNames` across app/src and app/test returns exactly two hits, both in model.ts (the definition at :193 and the single call inside buddyLabel at :201). BuddyList.tsx and Slips.tsx import/use only `buddyLabel`. A maintainer reading 'Shared by BuddyList and Slips' in six months will look for those consumers, find none, and distrust the whole comment block — the exact confusion a rename-left-behind comment causes. The `export` also implies an external contract that doesn't exist, widening the public surface for no consumer.
remediation: Update the comment to describe its real role, e.g. `/** person i's buddies as display names; the projection buddyLabel joins. */`, and drop `export` (make it a module-local `function buddyNames(...)`) since only buddyLabel calls it. If an external consumer is anticipated, keep the export but fix the 'Shared by BuddyList and Slips' claim, which is false today.
testUpgrade: Add a parameterized hygiene test (alongside app/test/hygiene.test.ts) that reads every `export`ed identifier from app/src/model.ts and asserts each is referenced in at least one file OTHER than model.ts (or is on an allowlist). This guards the CLASS 'exported-but-only-self-referenced symbol left by a refactor', so the next stray export/stale-'shared-by' comment fails CI instead of lingering.

summary: MAX_ROSTER_N's doc claims imports can display more people than generation allows, but the import cap equals the generation cap, so the claim is false and contradicts a documented safety invariant.
failure: The comment reads "(Import can display more — it only re-measures — but reroll is gated.)". But importGraph.ts:33 sets MAX_IMPORT_N = MAX_ROSTER_N and importGraph.ts:73 refuses f.people.length > MAX_IMPORT_N. So a 1001-person import is refused, not displayed; and any roster <=1000 rerolls without gating. Both halves of the parenthetical are stale. app/CLAUDE.md explicitly documents the OPPOSITE design: 'its size caps (MAX_IMPORT_N = MAX_ROSTER_N = 1000) match generation's ceiling ... the equality keeps the synchronous re-measure to a few hundred ms.' A contributor trusting this comment could raise MAX_IMPORT_N above MAX_ROSTER_N to 'allow display-only larger imports', reintroducing the main-thread O(n^2) re-measure freeze the equality was designed to prevent.
remediation: Replace the parenthetical with the actual invariant, e.g. '(Import is capped to the same ceiling — MAX_IMPORT_N = MAX_ROSTER_N — because import re-measures synchronously on the main thread; see importGraph.ts.)'
testUpgrade: Add to importExport.roundtrip (or a model invariant test) a parameterized assertion that MAX_IMPORT_N === MAX_ROSTER_N and that importGraph throws for people.length === MAX_ROSTER_N + 1, so the 'caps are equal' invariant is machine-guarded and the comment can't drift back to claiming import allows more.

summary: The 'frame the union of all modes so toggling pans but never rescales' invariant is defeated by computing forcePos lazily (null in ring mode), so the viewBox transform can rescale on every ring<->force toggle.
failure: Ring mode -> fit = computeFit(ringPos only), bbox exactly [-1,1]^2. Toggle to force -> forcePos materializes and fit = computeFit(ring union force). For a sparse graph where repulsion (forceManyBody strength -0.6) pushes any peripheral node outside the unit square, the union bbox grows, so at the toggle instant the still-ring display points are re-projected through a smaller scale s -- a visible rescale/pop before the 650ms pan. Toggling back to ring recomputes forcePos to null, collapsing the frame again, so it re-pops. This is exactly the mid-toggle rescale the union computation exists to prevent, and the F8 focus layout would inherit the already-broken invariant.
remediation: Make the force settle persist once computed so the union frame is stable across toggles: memoize forcePos on [n, edges] (not [layout, n, edges]) and gate only the WORK behind a 'force has been requested' ref, or compute a cheap force bounding box eagerly for fit alone. Alternatively, if per-mode tight framing is intended, drop the 'never rescales' claim from the comments so code and contract agree. Cost is low (memo-key change plus a compute-once ref); benefit is honoring the stated no-rescale contract and giving F8 a sound base. Visual only, hence suggestion not blocking.
testUpgrade: Parameterized: export computeFit and for several (n, edge-set) fixtures assert computeFit(ringPos) deep-equals computeFit([...ringPos, ...forceLayout(n,edges)]) -- force never enlarges the frame -- OR render GraphCanvas, snapshot the root <g> transform in ring mode, toggle ring->force->ring, and assert the transform on return equals the original for every fixture, so any mode that widens the frame is caught as a class.

summary: SEPARATION_DEFAULT re-exports the core's DEFAULT_MIN_SEPARATION but is never guaranteed to lie within the app-local [SEPARATION_MIN, SEPARATION_MAX] range it is used as an in-range fallback for, and nothing guards the coupling.
failure: SEPARATION_DEFAULT = DEFAULT_MIN_SEPARATION (currently 5, in range). It is used as the in-range fallback in SettingsControls.tsx:20 (invalid input -> SEPARATION_DEFAULT, bypassing the clamp), as the number input's default at SettingsControls.tsx:44 (rendered under min=SEPARATION_MIN/max=SEPARATION_MAX), and as sanitizeInt's fallback in importGraph.ts:48. If a future core change moves DEFAULT_MIN_SEPARATION outside [2,12] (e.g. to 1 or 15) — which the model.ts comment invites: 'if the core's default moves, this re-export moves with it' — then an invalid imported minSeparation silently falls back to an out-of-range value the stepper cannot express, and a reroll passes it straight to the core, breaking the very 'panel and import agree on one in-range default' invariant the comment claims. There is no test asserting SEPARATION_MIN <= SEPARATION_DEFAULT <= SEPARATION_MAX.
remediation: Either clamp at the definition — export const SEPARATION_DEFAULT = Math.max(SEPARATION_MIN, Math.min(SEPARATION_MAX, DEFAULT_MIN_SEPARATION)) — or add an explicit invariant test/assert so the re-export can't silently escape the UI range.
testUpgrade: Add a model invariant test asserting SEPARATION_MIN <= SEPARATION_DEFAULT <= SEPARATION_MAX (and likewise BUDDY_MIN <= DEFAULT_SETTINGS.buddies <= BUDDY_MAX), guarding the class of app-range-vs-re-exported-core-constant drift rather than the single current value 5.

summary: On an Edit->Generate that yields byte-identical edges under DIFFERENT settings, the kept view retains the OLD settings, so the exported file's settings block disagrees with what the user just configured (and with the Advanced panel).
failure: Roster of 5 with buddies=4 always produces K5. Generate with seed=1 (view.settings.seed=1). Open Edit, change Advanced seed to 2 (or change minSeparation), Generate again without editing the roster. useBuddyGraph's `sameStrings && sameEdges` branch keeps `cur` (the seed=1 view) and never calls setView, so bg.view.settings.seed stays 1. But App's `settings` state was set to 2 by handleGenerate, so SettingsControls shows seed=2 while exportGraph(view) writes seed=1. The exported determinism dial contradicts the UI and would drive a future reroll from the wrong base seed on re-import.
remediation: When the result is identical but `cur.settings` differs from `next.settings`, don't keep the stale object wholesale: swap in a view that carries `next.settings` while REUSING `cur.edges`/`cur.buddies` by reference (so GraphCanvas's `edges` identity is unchanged and no re-layout/animation is triggered). This preserves the no-relayout optimization the current branch is protecting while keeping the exported settings truthful. Only the reroll callback path (wasReroll) should remain a pure no-op.
testUpgrade: Class: 'displayed/exported settings must track the latest accepted generate even when the graph is visually unchanged.' Add a parameterized case to app/test/useBuddyGraph.test.tsx driving an identical-edges non-reroll generate across a table of changed-setting fields ({seed}, {minSeparation}, {polish}) and asserting result.current.view.settings equals the NEW settings (not the old), while also asserting view.edges === the prior edges reference (no re-layout). A companion export test (importExport.roundtrip) should assert exportGraph(view).settings mirrors the last generate's settings after such an idempotent regenerate.

summary: The FORCE_MAX_EDGES rationale comment claims only imports can trip the force caps and that generated graphs are 'far smaller', but a max-size generation exceeds FORCE_MAX_EDGES and silently falls back to ring in force mode.
failure: Generate at the app's own ceiling n=1000, k=BUDDY_MAX=12. buildBuddyGraph(1000,12,{polish:false}) returns 6000 edges (verified empirically: n*k/2). forceLayout's guard `edges.length > FORCE_MAX_EDGES (4000)` fires, so `forceLayout` returns `ringLayout(n)` — the Force toggle appears to do nothing for a graph the app itself just produced. The comment 'Generated graphs are far smaller; this guards imports' tells a future maintainer this branch is import-only, so they won't suspect a generated graph silently loses its force view.
remediation: Fix the comment to state the truth: generated graphs at the k=BUDDY_MAX corner reach n*BUDDY_MAX/2 edges (6000 at n=1000), which exceeds FORCE_MAX_EDGES=4000, so a max-settings generation also falls back to ring. Then make an intentional decision: either raise FORCE_MAX_EDGES to ceil(MAX_ROSTER_N*BUDDY_MAX/2)=6000 so the force view is available for every graph the app can generate, or keep the cap and document that dense large graphs are ring-only by design (and consider disabling/annotating the Force toggle in that case).
testUpgrade: Parameterize a layout test over k in [BUDDY_MIN..BUDDY_MAX] at n=MAX_ROSTER_N: build the graph, run forceLayout, and assert whether it settled (positions differ from ringLayout) vs fell back. Pin the boundary — e.g. assert FORCE_MAX_EDGES >= Math.ceil(MAX_ROSTER_N * BUDDY_MAX / 2) if the intent is 'force works for everything we generate', or explicitly assert the fallback for the dense corner if ring-only-at-scale is intended — so the caps and the comment can't drift from generation limits.

summary: POLISH_MAX_N=120 hand-mirrors the core's polish threshold, which the core hardcodes as a bare literal `n <= 120` inside the un-exported `resolveWantPolish` (lib/src/core/index.ts:310) — the two are bound only by a 'if the core's threshold moves, update this' comment, with no cross-check test.
failure: Suppose a future core change tunes auto-polish to `n <= 150` (edit resolveWantPolish). Nothing in the app fails to compile or test. rerollBlockReason (model.ts:187) still tells users with 121..150 people 'This group is too large to shuffle', and useBuddyGraph.generate (useBuddyGraph.ts:67) still downgrades polish=true to 'auto' above 120 — both now wrong, and both silently. The coincidental third literal FORCE_TICK_KNEE_N=120 (layout.ts:46), an unrelated force-tick concept, compounds the risk that someone 'consolidates' or edits the wrong 120.
remediation: Make it lib-first, per app/CLAUDE.md's 'if a number is missing, add it to the core' rule: export the polish threshold from the core (e.g. `export const AUTO_POLISH_MAX_N = 120;` used by resolveWantPolish) and set `POLISH_MAX_N = AUTO_POLISH_MAX_N` in model.ts. If exporting it now is out of scope, at minimum add a test that imports the core and asserts the boundary via observable behavior.
testUpgrade: Add an oracle-parity test parameterized over n at the boundary (POLISH_MAX_N-1, POLISH_MAX_N, POLISH_MAX_N+1): call buildBuddyGraph twice with different seeds and polish:'auto', and assert the edges differ iff n <= POLISH_MAX_N (auto-polish active). This pins POLISH_MAX_N to the core's actual behavior so a core threshold move breaks a red test instead of silently mis-wording reroll copy.

summary: LAYOUT_MODES is dual-purposed as BOTH the set of user-selectable render modes AND the set of layouts unioned for the stable fit frame (computeFit at lines 90-93). The in-code comment at line 17-18 claims a future F8 focus mode 'adds exactly one branch' to positionsFor, understating the change: focus positions are selection-dependent, so if focus is added to LAYOUT_MODES the union-fit at lines 90-93 will fold selection-dependent points into the fixed viewBox and rescale the frame on every selection change — defeating the very purpose of the union frame (a fixed viewBox that only pans, never rescales, mid-interaction). The app CLAUDE.md already notes focus is 'a selection-keyed layout, not just extending LayoutMode', but the GraphCanvas comment/data-model still presents it as a one-branch add.
failure: Land F8 focus by adding 'focus' to LAYOUT_MODES + a branch in positionsFor(): selecting a node recomputes focusPos, computeFit re-unions it, and the SVG viewBox scale jumps on each click/hover instead of staying fixed — the union-frame invariant (guarded by graphCanvasFit.test.ts) breaks for the selection-dependent mode.
remediation: Split the two roles before F8: keep a FIT_MODES subset (ring + force, the position-stable layouts that define the frame) separate from the full LAYOUT_MODES the toggle offers, and frame computeFit over FIT_MODES only. Update the line 17-18 comment to say a selection-keyed mode is added to positionsFor but deliberately excluded from the fit union. This is a small, localized change entirely within GraphCanvas — no cross-file contract change — so cost is low; doing it now (or at least documenting the split point in code, not only in CLAUDE.md) keeps the F8 seam genuinely open.
testUpgrade: Parameterize the graphCanvasFit union test over an added selection-dependent mock layout: assert computeFit's scale is invariant to changes in any layout NOT in the fit set (feed two different 'focus' position arrays and assert fit.s is unchanged), guarding the class 'selection-dependent positions must not perturb the fixed frame' rather than only today's ring+force pair.

summary: LAYOUT_MODES is exported as the single source of selectable layout modes and the documented F8-focus extension point, but has no runtime consumer — the App toggle hardcodes its buttons — so the OCP openness it advertises is fictional.
failure: Landing F8 focus per the in-code recipe ('add to LAYOUT_MODES and positionsFor'): adding 'focus' to LAYOUT_MODES surfaces no UI (App.tsx:148-151 hardcodes Ring/Force and imports only `type LayoutMode`, not LAYOUT_MODES), and positionsFor(layout, ringPos, forcePos) cannot see selected/hovered, so a focus branch forces a signature change across its 3 call sites (fit line 101 must NOT receive selection; target line 105 and animation line 124 must). The advertised single-branch add is not what the code allows.
remediation: Either make LAYOUT_MODES load-bearing by driving App's toggle from it (render one button per mode) so adding a mode genuinely opens the UI; or drop LAYOUT_MODES and keep the runtime-used FIT_MODES only. If focus is imminent, give positionsFor an explicit nullable selection parameter now (ignored by ring/force) so the fit vs target/animation call sites already differ intentionally. Cost is low (a few lines in App.tsx or deleting an unused export); benefit is a truthful seam. Not blocking — the feature still lands, just touching more files than the comment implies.
testUpgrade: Parameterized render test over LAYOUT_MODES asserting the layout toggle renders exactly one selectable control per mode (proving the abstraction is load-bearing); today no test exercises LAYOUT_MODES against the actual toggle DOM, only positionsFor in isolation.

summary: LAYOUT_MODES is only half load-bearing: the toggle button is data-driven, but its ACTIVE-state styling is hardcoded per mode in CSS (`.on.ring`/`.on.force`), so a future added mode surfaces a button whose selected state is invisible.
failure: Add a third entry to LAYOUT_MODES (e.g. "clusters") -> LayoutToggle renders a `clusters` button (correct), but selecting it applies only the generic `#toggle button.on` rule (color: var(--bg), a DARK ink) with no matching `.on.clusters { background }` rule. Result: dark text on the translucent-dark glass with no highlight — the active layout is visually indistinguishable from the inactive ones, contradicting the LayoutToggle comment's promise that 'adding a mode there surfaces its button (its CSS hook is the mode name)'. Current ring/force behavior is unaffected because both are explicitly styled.
remediation: Make the active-state background data-driven rather than per-mode: either a single generic `#toggle button.on { background: var(--accent) }` (with `--accent` optionally overridden per mode via a `[data-mode]`/class), or document that each LAYOUT_MODES entry REQUIRES a matching `.on.<mode>` rule and enforce it in a test. Minimal fix: give `#toggle button.on` a default visible background so an unstyled new mode still reads as selected.
testUpgrade: Class = 'every selectable mode is fully wired (button + reachable active styling)'. Add a parameterized CSS-parsing test (mirroring cssTokens.test.ts, which already reads app.css) that iterates LAYOUT_MODES and asserts each mode has a rule granting the active button a non-transparent `background` (e.g. a regex for `\.on\.<mode>\b[^}]*background` OR a generic `#toggle button.on` background). This turns red when a mode is added to LAYOUT_MODES without corresponding active styling — guarding the whole class, not just ring/force. The existing layoutToggle.test.tsx is too narrow: it only checks the className contains the mode name, never that CSS responds to that hook.

summary: The round-15 story is 'LAYOUT_MODES is the single load-bearing source of selectable layouts.' It is load-bearing for rendering a button, but the layout->positions resolver it feeds is NOT exhaustive, so a new mode added to LAYOUT_MODES compiles and renders a button that silently does nothing.
failure: Land the named next-milestone feature: add 'focus' to the LayoutMode union (line 6) and to LAYOUT_MODES (line 9). Where it catches: nowhere. positionsFor's ternary `layout === "force" ? (forcePos ?? ringPos) : ringPos` has a catch-all else, so 'focus' resolves to ringPos; forcePos's memo (`layout === "force"`) stays null; FIT_MODES is untouched. Result: LayoutToggle renders a third 'Focus' button (layoutToggle.test stays green), clicking it sets layout='focus', and the canvas silently shows the ring layout with no active-button highlight. The compiler never points at the ~4 sites (positionsFor, forcePos memo, FIT_MODES decision, CSS active rule) that actually need editing, so the 'add a mode to LAYOUT_MODES' seam the comment advertises produces a broken feature, not a working or a red one.
remediation: Make positionsFor exhaustive over LayoutMode: a `switch (layout)` whose default assigns `layout satisfies never` (or returns via an assertNever), so adding a member to the union forces a compile error at the exact resolver that must gain a branch. That converts the silent ring-fallback into a loud, single-seam edit and makes the 'load-bearing LAYOUT_MODES' claim true rather than aspirational.
testUpgrade: Parameterize over LAYOUT_MODES in graphCanvasFit/positionsFor: for every mode m, assert positionsFor(m, ring, force) is defined and, for any mode NOT in FIT_MODES, that it is selection-stable; plus a type-level test (expectTypeError) that removing a case from the switch fails to compile. This guards the CLASS (every declared mode has an intentional positions mapping) rather than just ring/force.

summary: The layout toggle is a mutually-exclusive selector (radio semantics) rendered as plain <button>s inside role=group, with the active mode conveyed ONLY through a CSS class (color/background). The selected state is invisible to assistive tech, against the app's stated 'keyboard-navigable / WCAG-AA' principle in app/CLAUDE.md.
failure: A screen-reader user tabs into the Layout group and hears 'Ring, button' then 'Force, button' with no indication which is active; after clicking, nothing announces the change of selection. grep confirms no aria-pressed/aria-current/role=radio anywhere in app/src.
remediation: Add `aria-pressed={layout === m}` to each button (toggle-button pattern) or switch to role=radiogroup + role=radio with aria-checked. One attribute, no structural change; the CSS `.on` hook stays for visuals.
testUpgrade: In layoutToggle.test.tsx, parameterize over LAYOUT_MODES: for each mode render with layout=m and assert exactly that button reports the selected state to AT (getByRole('button',{pressed:true}) is the m-th) and the others report unpressed — guarding the CLASS that selection is programmatically exposed for every mode, not just visually.

summary: LayoutToggle claims LAYOUT_MODES is the single load-bearing source of selectable layouts, but the active-button styling (background + glow) is hard-coded per mode in CSS, so adding a mode renders an invisible active state.
failure: Add "focus" to LAYOUT_MODES (the F8 step GraphCanvas.tsx:16-24 and app/CLAUDE.md explicitly set up). LayoutToggle renders a Focus button, but when selected it gets only `.on { color: var(--bg) }` (app.css:105, near-black #0a0e1a) with NO background/glow, because those come solely from `#toggle button.on.ring` / `#toggle button.on.force` (app.css:106-107). Result: near-black text on the dark `.glass` panel (app.css:82) — the active tab is effectively invisible, contradicting the comment's promise that adding a mode 'surfaces its button here'. layoutToggle.test.tsx passes because it only checks button count/label/`on` class, never a visible active style.
remediation: Make the active style data-driven to match the component: give `#toggle button.on` a generic background/glow driven by CSS custom properties (e.g. `background: var(--accent); box-shadow: 0 0 16px var(--accent-glow);`) and set `--accent`/`--accent-glow` per mode class, OR drive the accent from an inline style using a mode->color map co-located with LAYOUT_MODES. If per-mode CSS must stay, fix the comment to state that each new mode ALSO requires a `#toggle button.on.<mode>` rule (remove the 'single load-bearing source' overclaim).
testUpgrade: Parameterize a test over LAYOUT_MODES that reads app.css and asserts each mode has a matching active-state rule with a background (e.g. regex `#toggle button\.on\.<mode>\b[^}]*background`), so adding a mode without its CSS hook fails; alternatively render LayoutToggle with layout=m for every m and assert getComputedStyle(activeButton).backgroundColor is not transparent.

summary: The quality gauge (Math.round(quality*100)) and the connection caption ('loosely'/'well-linked') straddle the 0.5 threshold at different granularities, so the identical displayed number 50 can carry either caption.
failure: A connected graph with quality=0.499 renders gauge '50' with caption 'everyone's connected, but loosely linked'; quality=0.504 renders the identical gauge '50' with 'everyone's well-linked'. QualityPanel.tsx:17 does q=Math.round(m.quality*100) while connectionSummary (model.ts:135) compares the un-rounded quality against WELL_LINKED_QUALITY=0.5, so 50% maps to both captions. Reproduced: quality in [0.495,0.5) -> gauge 50 + 'loosely'; [0.5,0.505) -> gauge 50 + 'well-linked'.
remediation: Derive the caption from the same rounded integer the gauge shows (e.g. threshold on Math.round(quality*100) >= 50), or have QualityPanel pass the rounded value into connectionSummary, so the number and the words are computed from one quantity. This is cosmetic (a 50% score labelled 'loosely linked' is defensible), hence suggestion-level, but it is a genuine derived-number/caption divergence.
testUpgrade: Class: displayed-metric vs derived-caption consistency. Add a parameterized test in quality.test.ts (or a new captionConsistency.test.ts) that sweeps quality across the threshold — e.g. for q in [0.0,0.49,0.495,0.499,0.5,0.501,0.505,0.51,1.0] assert that Math.round(q*100) and connectionSummary agree in tier (any gauge >=50 pairs with 'well-linked', any <50 with 'loosely'), so a future copy/threshold change that reintroduces a same-number-two-captions straddle turns the test red. The existing quality.test.ts only checks endpoint captions, not the rounding boundary, so it is too narrow to have caught this.

summary: LARGE_ROSTER is `export`ed but referenced only inside feasibility.ts — a dead export the hygiene test doesn't catch because that test only scans model.ts.
failure: grep LARGE_ROSTER across app/ returns exactly two hits, both in feasibility.ts (the declaration line 4 and its sole use line 47). A maintainer sees `export const LARGE_ROSTER` and assumes a panel or test consumes the 300-person 'large group' threshold; nothing does, so they burn time hunting a phantom consumer (and may keep it in sync with a value nobody reads).

testUpgrade: Generalize the hygiene.test.ts 'every exported symbol has an external consumer' check from model.ts only to every module under app/src — walk each *.ts/*.tsx, extract `export (function|const) NAME`, and assert NAME appears in at least one OTHER src/test file. That turns any future orphan export (not just model's) red.

summary: `<details className="advanced">` carries a class hook that no rule in app.css or print.css ever targets — an orphan className (likely left by a rename/removed rule).
failure: grep for `.advanced` / `advanced` across app/src/styles returns zero CSS rules; the only occurrence is this JSX attribute. A contributor styling the Advanced disclosure will add a `.advanced { … }` rule expecting it to already be wired (it is), or conversely will assume the class is load-bearing and preserve it during cleanup — either way the hook silently does nothing today.

testUpgrade: Add a cssTokens/hygiene-style test that collects every `className="…"` literal token used in app/src/**/*.tsx and every class selector defined in app/src/styles/*.css, and asserts no JSX class token is entirely unreferenced by CSS (allowlist genuinely-behavioral hooks like state classes if needed) — guarding the class of orphaned style hooks.

summary: LAYOUT_MODES and FIT_MODES are exported as mutable `LayoutMode[]`; being the single load-bearing source of selectable/frameable modes, they should be immutable so a consumer can't mutate the app's mode set.
failure: `import { LAYOUT_MODES } from './GraphCanvas'; LAYOUT_MODES.push('focus' as any)` compiles and mutates shared module state, changing which buttons LayoutToggle renders app-wide. The arrays are described as 'the single, load-bearing source' yet are freely reassignable in place.
remediation: Declare them `export const LAYOUT_MODES = ["ring", "force"] as const satisfies readonly LayoutMode[];` (and same for FIT_MODES), and type consumers as `readonly LayoutMode[]`. This keeps the exhaustiveness/derivation benefits while making the public surface hard to misuse.
testUpgrade: Add a type-level test (expectTypeOf / a `// @ts-expect-error` on `LAYOUT_MODES.push(...)`) asserting the exported mode arrays are `readonly`, guarding against a future export of a mutable app-wide constant.

summary: The duplicate-removal warning keys its list on the current occurrence's casing, so multiple case-variants of ONE person are listed as if they were distinct names.
failure:
Input "Alice
alice
ALICE
Bob" correctly yields names ["Alice","Bob"], but the warning reads "Removed 2 duplicate entries (alice, ALICE). Each person appears once." — the parenthetical lists two different spellings of the single already-kept person "Alice", which reads as two separate duplicated names rather than two extra copies of one. The dropped COUNT (2) is correct; only the name list is misleading.
remediation: Key `extras` on the case-insensitive key (or map back to the first-kept display name via a `key -> keptName` lookup) so each de-duplicated person appears once in the list, e.g. store `extras` under `key` and display the originally-kept casing. Behavior (names array, count) is already correct; this is wording only.
testUpgrade: Add a parameterized case to app/test/parseRoster.test.ts covering the CLASS 'same person, mixed casing, multiple extra copies': assert (a) names dedupe to the first-seen casing, (b) the reported dropped count equals total extra copies, and (c) each distinct person appears at most once in the warning's parenthetical (regex count of comma-separated entries == number of distinct de-duplicated people), with rows like ["Alice/alice/ALICE"], ["Bob,BOB,bob,Bob"], and a mix of two different duplicated people to guard against both under- and over-listing.

summary: `Metrics.girth` is documented as a "Display metric" and is computed on every import via an O(n^2) `girth(g)` call, but no component renders it — QualityPanel shows only aspl, diameter, and the quality gauge.
failure: Import (or generate) any graph -> `girth(g)` runs (uncapped O(n^2), up to MAX_IMPORT_N=1000 on the main thread) and is carried through RawMetrics -> Metrics -> the export `meta.metrics` block, yet grep shows `.girth` is never read by any panel/logic. A contributor reading model.ts's "Display metrics" heading either wastes time hunting the nonexistent render or re-adds a girth row that already exists in the model, and the import pays a quadratic pass to fill a field only ever written to a file's write-only meta snapshot.
remediation: Pick one: (a) surface girth in QualityPanel if it's meant to be shown; or (b) drop `girth` from `Metrics`/`RawMetrics`, remove the `girth(g)` call in importGraph.ts:155 and `girth: r.girth` in viewFromResult, ending the quadratic import cost; or (c) if it is deliberately kept only for the exported meta snapshot, retitle the interface doc from "Display metrics" to note girth is carried in the exported meta snapshot and NOT shown in the UI.
testUpgrade: Parameterized test that renders QualityPanel for a representative Metrics and asserts each numeric Metrics field is either present in the rendered output OR listed in an explicit `EXPORT_ONLY` allowlist — so any future display-metric added to `Metrics` but forgotten in the UI (or any field silently orphaned) fails the test.

summary: `readFileText(file, maxBytes = MAX_FILE_BYTES)` exposes a `maxBytes` override that no call site (App.tsx:105, RosterModal.tsx:44) and no test ever passes — dead parameter surface.
failure: grep for `readFileText(` across app/src and app/test finds only the two production callers, both single-arg, and no direct test of the size gate. The override is neither exercised nor needed, so a maintainer can't tell whether it's a live testing seam or vestigial, and the byte-gate's rejection branch is currently untested.
remediation: Either inline `MAX_FILE_BYTES` and drop the parameter, or add a unit test that passes a small `maxBytes` and asserts the oversized-file rejection message — turning the seam into a covered one.
testUpgrade: Test that `readFileText(new File([bigString], 'x'), tinyLimit)` rejects with the "too large" message and that an under-limit file resolves, parameterized over a couple of (size, limit) pairs to guard the gate class.

summary: The reroll "already an optimal arrangement" message gates on raw `kept.metrics.quality === 1`, a third quality-derived UI string that bypasses the `qualityPercent` seam model.ts advertises as the single source for all quality-derived copy (gauge + caption).
failure: Not a live bug today (quality===1 implies qualityPercent===100). But the coupling is an uncommented invariant: if clampQuality's rounding changes or qualityPercent later renders a decimal, the optimal claim can desync from a gauge reading 100; conversely a future contributor "unifying" this to `qualityPercent===100` would then falsely claim optimality at 99.6% (a plateau a reroll could still improve).
remediation: Add an `isOptimal(m: Metrics): boolean` helper in model.ts beside qualityPercent (returns `m.quality === 1`) and call it here, so every quality-derived UI string shares one seam and the "never claim optimal below a full gauge" invariant lives in one commented place.
testUpgrade: Property test over quality in [0.9, 1.0]: assert the optimal-arrangement copy is chosen iff `isOptimal(m)` AND `qualityPercent(m) === 100`, i.e. no gauge value below 100 ever pairs with the optimal claim.

summary: The "try example names" button (and any setText path that bypasses capText) never clears inputCapped or fileError, so a truncation/read-error notice lingers over unrelated, valid roster text.
failure: In one open modal session: paste >500,000 chars -> capText sets inputCapped=true and the "only the first 500,000 characters were kept" note renders. Then click "try example names" (line 78 calls setText(SAMPLE_NAMES.join("\n")) directly, bypassing capText). Text is now ~a dozen sample names, but inputCapped stays true, so the truncation note is still shown for text that wasn't truncated. Same class: drop an unreadable/oversized file (setFileError set, line 45-47) then click "try example names" -> the red file-error note persists over the valid sample text (fileError is only cleared at the start of readFile, line 43, never by the example/textarea-clear paths).
remediation: Route the example button (and treat it as an explicit user text-set) through the same reset the file/textarea paths use: on setting sample text, call capText (or setInputCapped(false)) and setFileError(null). Simplest: a setRoster(s: string) helper that does setText(capText(s)); setFileError(null); and have both the onChange, readFile-success, and example button call it, so transient notices can never outlive the text they described.
testUpgrade: Class: transient RosterModal notices (inputCapped truncation, fileError) must be cleared by every text-replacing action, not just the one that raised them. Add a parameterized RTL test over the state-transition matrix {raise via: huge paste, oversized-file reject} x {clear via: type new text, click try-example, choose valid file}: after the clear action, assert neither the truncation note nor the file-error note is in the document. This also guards the initialText path (a >500k-char initialText should render without falsely asserting it was capped). Existing rosterModalTruncation.test.tsx only exercises the raise path, so it wouldn't catch this.

summary: The char-truncation warning parseRoster pushes is unreachable via every production caller and duplicates RosterModal's notice with divergent wording ("read" vs "kept").
failure: Both real callers pre-gate the char count: RosterModal.capText (RosterModal.tsx:34-38) slices input to exactly MAX_PARSE_CHARS before calling parseRoster, and importGraph.ts:119 throws when joined.length > MAX_PARSE_CHARS before ever calling parseRoster. So parseRoster.ts's `characters were read` warning reaches a user through NO path — only the near-identical RosterModal.tsx:104 `characters were kept` copy is ever shown. A maintainer reweaving the user-facing truncation wording edits parseRoster.ts:34 (guided by the parseRoster.ts:26 comment `truncated (with a warning)`), ships it, and no user sees the change while the two strings silently diverge.
remediation: Extract one shared truncation-copy constant/helper used by both RosterModal and parseRoster, OR drop parseRoster's warning push (keep the char cap) and let each caller own its notice; and correct the parseRoster.ts:26 comment to state the warning is for direct API callers only, not the app UI.
testUpgrade: Parameterized test that the truncation string surfaced to the user (RosterModal) and any parseRoster char-cap warning both derive from a single shared MAX_PARSE_CHARS-keyed constant — assert the two produced strings are equal (or one source), so rewording one place fails until both agree.

summary: The file-size gate enforces 8 MiB (8*1024*1024 B) but the rejection message and comment call it "8 MB" while dividing sizes by 1e6, so the stated limit differs from the enforced one.
failure: MAX_FILE_BYTES = 8*1024*1024 = 8,388,608 B, but the error text prints `limit ${Math.floor(maxBytes/1e6)} MB` = "8 MB" and reports file size as size/1e6. A 8,350,000-byte file (over "8 MB" by the same 1e6 divisor the message uses) is ACCEPTED, and a rejected 8,400,000-byte file reads "8.4 MB; limit 8 MB" — a stated ceiling 0.39 MB below the real one. Files in (8,000,000, 8,388,608] bytes pass despite exceeding the named 8 MB.
remediation: Pick one unit: either set MAX_FILE_BYTES = 8_000_000 and keep the /1e6 formatting, or display MiB (divide by 1024*1024 and label "MiB") so the printed limit equals the enforced boundary.
testUpgrade: Property test over sizes around the cap asserting the numeric limit parsed back out of the rejection message is >= the largest accepted file size and < the smallest rejected size (no gap between the stated and enforced limit).

summary: The generation pipeline hard-wires failure == thrown-error; the named next feature (constraints) needs a third 'refused-with-reasons' notion that the request/response contract, the worker, useBuddyGraph, and viewFromResult cannot express without a coordinated multi-file edit. (Documented in app/CLAUDE.md as a deliberate deferral; surfaced to name where the constraints extension catches. Not blocking.)
failure: Landing a require_same/constraints feature: buildConstrainedBuddyGraph refuses on a SUCCESSFUL return via report.refusals (not a throw), but GenerateResponse (protocol.ts:23-25) only models {ok:true,result}|{ok:false,error}; generate.worker.ts:13-18 collapses all failure into catch; viewFromResult (model.ts:246) always sets connected:true/fraction:1 and has no constrained variant; Settings/GenerateOptions carry no constraint fields. So one feature edits protocol.ts + generate.worker.ts + useGenerationWorker + useBuddyGraph + model.ts together — a cross-file contract change, exactly the OCP seam the brief asks about.
remediation: When F7 lands (not now — YAGNI), widen GenerateResponse to a third variant {ok:false,refused:true,reasons:string[],partial?:BuddyResult}, branch the worker to buildConstrainedBuddyGraph, and give viewFromResult a constrained producer that reads the report's connectivity instead of asserting it. The schema already reserves constraints, so only the runtime contract needs the widening.
testUpgrade: Parameterize a worker-protocol test over response kind (ok | error-thrown | refused-with-reasons) asserting useBuddyGraph maps each to a distinct UI state, so a future 'failure==throw only' regression fails the class.

summary: handleReroll embeds the reroll-feasibility decision (seed advance + feasibility() + rerollBlockReason() + dispatch) inline in the composition root, so App owns both wiring and a piece of generation-eligibility policy. Borderline and low-cost; not blocking.
failure: A next reasonable change — e.g. adding a new pre-hoc reroll block reason (constraints make this roster uniquely determined) or reusing the same gate for an auto-reroll affordance — must edit App.tsx's handler body rather than a single policy unit, and the gate has no direct unit test (only rerollBlockReason/feasibility are tested in isolation, not their App-level composition).
remediation: Extract the reroll gate into a small pure function or useReroll hook (advance seed -> feasibility -> rerollBlockReason -> {dispatch|reason}) that App calls, keeping App as pure composition and giving the gate a direct test seam.
testUpgrade: A table-driven test over (n, settings) -> {dispatched | blockedReason} for the reroll gate, covering too-large, polish-off, feasible, and infeasible-k rows, so a new block reason ratchets in as a case rather than living untested inside a component handler.

summary: The status="error" branch is handled with a persistent notice but the recovery paths around it are incomplete: a first-generation error leaves the user with no modal and no view (dead-end), and a later error's toast is never cleared when an import supersedes it.
failure: If buildBuddyGraph ever throws for a dispatched job: (a) on the FIRST generation, handleGenerate has already set modalOpen=false and view stays null, so main renders neither the view block (which holds "Edit people") nor the modal, and the busy overlay's Cancel is gone (status is "error", not "running") -> the user is stuck with only an error toast and no affordance to retry. (b) With a view present, the error effect calls show(bg.error) (persistent, not flash), and applyImported/loadView never clear the notice, so after a successful import the stale red error toast lingers over the fresh graph. NOTE: I verified a 55-combo (n,k,minSeparation) sweep plus n=1000 never throws for feasibility-gated inputs (MAX_CACHED_N=5000 > app cap 1000), so this branch is currently unreachable through the UI -- it is a latent gap in code that is written to run, not a reproduced live defect.
remediation: On status="error", also reopen the modal when there is no view (mirror cancelGeneration's `if (!view) setModalOpen(true)`), and clear the notice in loadView/applyImported (or have the status effect clear on status==="idle"/"done") so a superseding import doesn't leave a stale error toast.
testUpgrade: Class: worker-failure recovery. Add a useBuddyGraph/App test that injects gen.status="error" (the existing useGenerationWorker mock already exposes settable state) and asserts (1) with view===null the modal is re-openable, and (2) after loadView/import the notice is cleared. Parameterize over {first-gen error, error-then-import, error-then-successful-reroll} so all recovery transitions are guarded, not just the happy path currently covered in useBuddyGraph.test.tsx.

summary: The first-generation error recovery gates BOTH the toast and the modal reopen on `bg.error` being truthy, so a worker error whose message string is empty ("") would skip recovery entirely — no toast and no reopened modal on a first generation, leaving a blank screen.
failure: If the worker returns `{ok:false, error:""}` while `view===null`, the effect's `bg.status === "error" && bg.error` condition is false (empty string is falsy), so `setModalOpen(true)` never runs and the user is stranded with no graph, no modal, and no toast. Not reachable from current hostile input (the gated core throws Error objects with non-empty messages, and this branch is documented-defensive), hence PLAUSIBLE not CONFIRMED.
remediation: Decouple the modal-reopen from the message's truthiness: branch on `bg.status === "error"` alone, reopen the modal when `!view` regardless, and only call `show(bg.error)` when a message exists (or fall back to a generic 'Generation failed' string). e.g. `if (bg.status === "error") { show(bg.error || "Generation failed."); if (!view) setModalOpen(true); }`.
testUpgrade: In appErrorRecovery.test.tsx, parameterize the first-generation-error case over a table of error payloads — `"Generation failed"`, `""`, and a whitespace-only string — asserting the setup modal reopens (no dead-end) for every non-view error regardless of message content, so the whole class of empty/blank worker messages is guarded rather than the one happy-path string.
